### `discussion_board_ban_records`

Audit trail of user ban actions with reasons, timestamps, and
administrator attribution.

This table tracks all user suspension actions on the discussion board
platform. Each record captures when a user was banned, the reason for the
ban, which administrator imposed it, and when (if ever) the ban was
lifted.

The table uses a polymorphic ownership pattern to support banning both
members and administrators. The actor_type field distinguishes between
the two actor types, with separate subtype tables
(discussion_board_ban_record_of_members and
discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators) maintaining the actual
foreign key relationships.

Key relationships:
- [discussion_board_administrators](#discussion_board_administrators): Administrator who imposed the ban
- [discussion_board_ban_record_of_members](#discussion_board_ban_record_of_members): Member-specific ban
details (1:1)
- [discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators](#discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators):
Administrator-specific ban details (1:1)

This table serves as the authoritative record for moderation
accountability and enforcement history.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `banned_by`
  > Administrator who imposed the ban. {@link
  > discussion_board_administrators.id}.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor being banned. Either 'member' or 'administrator'. Used with
  > subtype tables for polymorphic ownership.
- `ban_reason`
  > Required reason explaining why the user was banned. Must contain detailed
  > explanation of policy violation or harmful behavior.
- `banned_at`
  > Timestamp when the ban was imposed. Recorded automatically when ban
  > action is executed.
- `unbanned_at`: Timestamp when the ban was lifted. Null if the ban is still active.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this ban record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this ban record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this ban record was soft deleted. Used for audit trail
  > preservation.

### `discussion_board_ban_record_of_members`

Subtype table for member ban records implementing polymorphic ownership
pattern.

This table links ban records to specific member accounts with a 1:1
relationship. It is part of the polymorphic ownership design where ban
records can apply to different actor types (members or administrators)
through separate subtype tables.

**Key Characteristics**:
- Each ban record references exactly one member via unique foreign key
- Each member can have at most one active ban record
- Stores the session information of the administrator who performed the
ban for audit trail
- No duplicate temporal fields - accessed via parent ban record

**Relationships**:
- [discussion_board_ban_records.id](#discussion_board_ban_records) - Parent ban record (1:1)
- [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) - Banned member account (1:1)
- [discussion_board_administrator_sessions.id](#discussion_board_administrator_sessions) - Session of
administrator who performed the ban (optional, for audit)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_ban_record_id`
  > Parent ban record's [discussion_board_ban_records.id](#discussion_board_ban_records). Establishes
  > 1:1 relationship with the main ban record entity.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Banned member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Links the ban record
  > to the specific member account being banned.
- `discussion_board_administrator_session_id`
  > Administrator session's {@link
  > discussion_board_administrator_sessions.id} that performed the ban
  > action. Used for audit trail to track which administrator session
  > executed the ban.

### `discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators`

Subtype table linking ban records to administrator accounts.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for ban records,
specifically handling cases where an administrator account is banned. It
maintains a 1:1 relationship with the main ban record entity, ensuring
each ban record is associated with exactly one actor type.

The table stores the reference to the banned administrator's account,
enabling proper tracking of which administrator was suspended, while the
main ban record stores the reason, timestamp, and banning administrator.

**Key Relationships**:
- Links to [discussion_board_ban_records.id](#discussion_board_ban_records) with unique constraint
(1:1)
- References [discussion_board_administrators.id](#discussion_board_administrators) for the banned
administrator

**Usage Pattern**:
- Created when an administrator is banned
- Maintains audit trail of administrator suspensions
- Works in conjunction with discussion_board_ban_record_of_members for
complete ban tracking

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_ban_record_id`: Reference to the main ban record. [discussion_board_ban_records.id](#discussion_board_ban_records)
- `discussion_board_administrator_id`
  > Reference to the banned administrator account. {@link

### `discussion_board_tags`

Master table storing unique tag names for article categorization and
filtering.

This table maintains the canonical list of all tags used across the
discussion board system. Each tag represents a free-text label that can
be assigned to articles for organizational purposes. Tags are created
dynamically when users assign them to articles, with no predefined
vocabulary or approval process required.

Key characteristics:
- Tags are free-text with no length restrictions
- Tag names are case-sensitive and preserve exact user input
- Multiple articles can share the same tag
- Tags exist independently of articles and persist even when all
associated articles are deleted
- Used for article filtering, search, and categorization across the platform

Related entities:
- [discussion_board_article_tags](#discussion_board_article_tags): Junction table linking tags to
articles (many-to-many relationship)
- [discussion_board_articles](#discussion_board_articles): Articles that can have multiple tags
assigned

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > The tag name as entered by the user. Preserves exact text including
  > capitalization and spacing. No predefined vocabulary or validation
  > against allowed values.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this tag was first created and added to the system.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this tag was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this tag was soft deleted. Null indicates the tag is
  > active.

### `discussion_board_article_tags`

Junction table for the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags.

This table enables free-text tag assignment to articles for
categorization, filtering, and search functionality. Each record
represents a single tag assignment to an article.

Key characteristics:

- **M:N Relationship**: Links [discussion_board_articles](#discussion_board_articles) to {@link
discussion_board_tags}
- **No Duplicates**: Composite unique constraint prevents assigning the
same tag to an article multiple times
- **Tag Filtering**: Supports filtering articles by specific tags
- **Audit Trail**: Created_at timestamp tracks when tags were assigned

Usage patterns:

- When creating an article with tags, insert records into this table
- When editing article tags, delete old assignments and insert new ones
- When deleting an article, all associated records are cascade-deleted

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > References the article this tag is assigned to. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}
- `discussion_board_tag_id`
  > References the tag assigned to this article. {@link
  > discussion_board_tags.id}
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this tag was assigned to the article.

# API Interface Requirements

## User Account APIs
- Sign up with email and password
- Log in with email and password
- Change password
- Delete account

## User Profile APIs
- View own profile
- Edit display name and bio
- View other users' profiles
- View articles written by a user
- View comments written by a user

## Sections APIs
- View list of all sections
- Browse articles within a specific section
- Create, edit, delete sections (admin only)

## Articles APIs
- Create article in a section
- Edit own article
- Delete own article
- View list of articles in a section (paginated, sortable)
- View single article
- Delete any article (admin only)

## Search APIs
- Search articles by title or content (paginated)
- Filter articles by tags

## Comments APIs
- Write comment on article
- View all comments on article
- Edit own comment
- Delete own comment
- Delete any comment (admin only)

## Administrator APIs
- Submit request to become administrator
- View list of pending requests (super admin only)
- Approve/reject requests (super admin only)
- Promote regular admin to super admin (super admin only)
- Demote super admin to regular admin (super admin only)
- Ban users (admin only)
- Unban users (admin only)
- View list of banned users (admin only)

operations.specification: Implementation creates a new guest identity based on device fingerprint from the request. Query the discussion_board_guests table for existing guest with matching device_fingerprint. If found, use existing guest record; if not found, create new guest with device_fingerprint and current timestamp. Create a new session record in discussion_board_guest_sessions with guest reference, IP address, current URL (href), referrer, created_at timestamp, and expired_at timestamp (30 minutes from now). Generate JWT access token (short-lived, e.g., 15 minutes) and refresh token (longer-lived, e.g., 30 minutes). Store tokens in session record. Return authorized response with both tokens. Handle edge cases: duplicate device fingerprints (reuse existing guest), session expiration (create new session), rate limiting per device fingerprint.
operations.description:
This API operation creates a new guest identity and authentication session for unauthenticated visitors to the discussion board platform. Guests are temporary users who can browse sections and view public articles without providing email or password credentials.

The operation identifies guests by device fingerprint, which is a unique identifier derived from browser characteristics (user-agent, screen resolution, installed fonts, etc.). When a guest first visits the platform, their device fingerprint is used to create or retrieve a guest record in the discussion_board_guests table. This table stores the device_fingerprint as a unique constraint, along with created_at and updated_at timestamps for audit purposes.

Upon successful guest creation or retrieval, a new session is established in the discussion_board_guest_sessions table. This session record captures connection metadata including the client's IP address for security auditing, the current URL (href) as the entry point, and the referrer URL for traffic source tracking. The session includes created_at timestamp for session start and expired_at timestamp for automatic expiration (typically 30 minutes of inactivity).

The operation returns JWT tokens in the IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized response format. The access token is short-lived (typically 15 minutes) for secure API access, while the refresh token is longer-lived (typically 30 minutes) to allow token renewal without re-authentication. These tokens enable the guest to browse sections and view public articles during their session.

Security considerations include rate limiting based on device fingerprint to prevent abuse, IP address logging for security monitoring, and automatic session expiration to limit exposure of stale tokens. The append-only nature of the discussion_board_guest_sessions table ensures an audit trail of all guest access attempts.

requestBody.description: Guest registration information including device fingerprint for identification

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for guest session access

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation validates the refresh token from the request. Query discussion_board_guest_sessions table for a session with matching refresh token that has not expired (expired_at > current time). Verify the session's guest reference exists in discussion_board_guests table. Generate new JWT access token (short-lived, e.g., 15 minutes) and optionally a new refresh token if token rotation is enabled. Update the session record's expired_at timestamp to extend the session lifetime. Return authorized response with new tokens. Handle edge cases: expired refresh token (401 Unauthorized), invalid refresh token (401 Unauthorized), deleted guest record (401 Unauthorized), session already expired (401 Unauthorized).
operations.description:
This API operation renews the authentication tokens for an existing guest session without requiring re-authentication. Guests use this endpoint to extend their session when the access token is about to expire but they are still actively browsing the platform.

The operation validates the refresh token provided in the request against the discussion_board_guest_sessions table. This table stores session records with their associated refresh tokens, expiration timestamps (expired_at), and references to the guest identity in discussion_board_guests. The validation process checks that the refresh token exists, has not expired, and belongs to a valid guest record.

Upon successful validation, the operation generates a new access token (typically valid for 15 minutes) and may generate a new refresh token if token rotation security policy is enabled. The session's expired_at timestamp is updated to extend the session lifetime, typically adding another 30 minutes of validity from the current time. This allows guests to maintain continuous access while browsing sections and viewing public articles.

The operation returns IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized response containing the new access token and refresh token. These tokens replace the expired tokens in the client's storage, enabling continued API access without interrupting the user's browsing experience.

Security considerations include token rotation to limit the window of exposure if a refresh token is compromised, session expiration to automatically terminate stale sessions, and validation against the discussion_board_guest_sessions table to ensure only legitimate sessions can be refreshed. Expired or invalid refresh tokens result in 401 Unauthorized responses, requiring the client to re-authenticate via the join endpoint.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for session renewal

responseBody.description: Renewed authentication tokens for guest session

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new member account in the discussion_board_members table. The implementation must:

1. Validate the email format and check for uniqueness in the discussion_board_members table
2. Hash the password using a secure algorithm (bcrypt or similar) before storage
3. Create a new member record with email, hashed password, and current timestamp for createdAt
4. Generate initial JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration
5. Create a corresponding session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table
6. Return the tokens in the IAuthorized response

Error handling:
- Return 400 Bad Request if email format is invalid
- Return 409 Conflict if email already exists in discussion_board_members
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database or token generation failures
operations.description:
This API operation allows new users to register as members on the discussion board platform. Upon successful registration, the member account is created in the discussion_board_members table with the provided email address and securely hashed password.

The registration process validates the email format for correctness and ensures uniqueness across all existing members. Once validation passes, the password is hashed using industry-standard cryptographic algorithms before being stored in the database, ensuring that plaintext passwords are never persisted.

After successful account creation, the system automatically generates JWT (JSON Web Token) access and refresh tokens for the new member. These tokens are stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table and returned to the client, enabling immediate authenticated access to member-only features without requiring a separate login step.

The response includes both access and refresh tokens following the IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized structure.

requestBody.description: Registration information for new member account including email and password

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the newly registered member

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates an existing member by validating their credentials against the discussion_board_members table. The implementation must:

1. Query the discussion_board_members table for a member with the provided email
2. Verify the member exists and is not banned (check discussion_board_ban_record_of_members if applicable)
3. Compare the provided password with the stored hashed password using secure comparison
4. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful authentication
5. Update or create a session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table
6. Return the tokens in the IAuthorized response

Error handling:
- Return 401 Unauthorized if email not found or password incorrect
- Return 403 Forbidden if member account is banned
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database or token generation failures
operations.description:
This API operation enables registered members to authenticate and gain access to the discussion board platform. The login process validates the member's credentials by querying the discussion_board_members table and comparing the provided password against the securely stored hash.

Upon successful credential validation, the system generates new JWT access and refresh tokens for the authenticated member. These tokens are stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table to maintain session state and enable token refresh operations. The tokens are then returned to the client for use in subsequent authenticated requests.

The operation also checks whether the member account has been banned by examining the discussion_board_ban_record_of_members table. If a ban record exists and is active, the login attempt is rejected with a 403 Forbidden response, preventing banned users from accessing the platform.

The response includes both access and refresh tokens following the IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized structure, enabling immediate authenticated access to member features.

requestBody.description: Login credentials including email and password

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the logged-in member

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation refreshes the authentication tokens for an existing member session. The implementation must:

1. Validate the provided refresh token against the discussion_board_member_sessions table
2. Verify the refresh token is valid, not expired, and belongs to an active member
3. Check that the associated member account exists and is not banned
4. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens
5. Update the session record in discussion_board_member_sessions with the new tokens and timestamps
6. Return the new tokens in the IAuthorized response

Error handling:
- Return 401 Unauthorized if refresh token is invalid, expired, or not found
- Return 403 Forbidden if member account is banned
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database or token generation failures
operations.description:
This API operation allows members to obtain new authentication tokens without requiring re-authentication with credentials. The token refresh mechanism is essential for maintaining long-lived sessions while keeping access tokens short-lived for security purposes.

The operation validates the provided refresh token against the discussion_board_member_sessions table to ensure it is valid, not expired, and associated with an active member account. If the refresh token is valid, the system generates new JWT access and refresh tokens and updates the session record with the new tokens and current timestamp.

This approach provides several security benefits: access tokens can be kept short-lived to minimize the window of opportunity for token theft, while refresh tokens enable seamless session continuation without requiring users to re-enter credentials. The refresh token validation also includes checks for account ban status to ensure banned users cannot continue their sessions.

The response includes both new access and refresh tokens following the IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized structure.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authentication tokens

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens for the member session

This operation creates a new administrator record in the discussion_board_administrators table with the provided email, hashed password, and optional display name and bio. The email must be unique across all administrator accounts as enforced by the unique constraint on the email column. Upon successful registration, the administrator is assigned a 'regular' grade by default and can immediately log in to access administrative features.

The password is hashed using a secure algorithm before storage in the password_hash column. The created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically set to record the account creation time. The administrator starts with no active sessions until they log in.

This operation is public and does not require authentication, allowing new administrators to register themselves. After registration, the administrator should use the login operation to obtain JWT tokens for authenticated access to protected resources.

The session includes connection metadata (IP address, href, referrer) for security auditing. This operation is public and does not require prior authentication. The returned tokens enable the administrator to access protected administrative resources and manage content, users, and system settings.

This operation validates the refresh token against the discussion_board_administrator_sessions table by comparing the token hash with the stored refresh_token_hash. If valid and not expired, a new access token is generated and the session's access_token_expires_at timestamp is updated.

The refresh token itself remains valid until its expiration time (typically 7 days from initial login). This allows administrators to maintain continuous access without re-entering credentials. The operation also validates that the session has not been terminated (expired_at is null).

This operation is public but requires a valid refresh token. It enables seamless token renewal for administrators who have an active session, preventing authentication interruptions during extended administrative work sessions.

1. Validate the email format and check for uniqueness in the discussion_board_members table
2. Hash the password using a secure algorithm (bcrypt or similar) before storage
3. Create a new member record with email, hashed password, and current timestamp for createdAt
4. Generate initial JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration
5. Create a corresponding session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table
6. Return the tokens in the IAuthorized response

Error handling:
- Return 400 Bad Request if email format is invalid
- Return 409 Conflict if email already exists in discussion_board_members
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database or token generation failures
operations.description:
This API operation allows new users to register as members on the discussion board platform. Upon successful registration, the member account is created in the discussion_board_members table with the provided email address and securely hashed password.

The registration process validates the email format for correctness and ensures uniqueness across all existing members. Once validation passes, the password is hashed using industry-standard cryptographic algorithms before being stored in the database, ensuring that plaintext passwords are never persisted.

After successful account creation, the system automatically generates JWT (JSON Web Token) access and refresh tokens for the new member. These tokens are stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table and returned to the client, enabling immediate authenticated access to member-only features without requiring a separate login step.

The response includes both access and refresh tokens following the IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized structure.

requestBody.description: Registration information for new member account including email and password

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the newly registered member

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates an existing member by validating their credentials against the discussion_board_members table. The implementation must:

1. Query the discussion_board_members table for a member with the provided email
2. Verify the member exists and is not banned (check discussion_board_ban_record_of_members if applicable)
3. Compare the provided password with the stored hashed password using secure comparison
4. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful authentication
5. Update or create a session record in discussion_board_member_sessions table
6. Return the tokens in the IAuthorized response

Error handling:
- Return 401 Unauthorized if email not found or password incorrect
- Return 403 Forbidden if member account is banned
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database or token generation failures
operations.description:
This API operation enables registered members to authenticate and gain access to the discussion board platform. The login process validates the member's credentials by querying the discussion_board_members table and comparing the provided password against the securely stored hash.

Upon successful credential validation, the system generates new JWT access and refresh tokens for the authenticated member. These tokens are stored in the discussion_board_member_sessions table to maintain session state and enable token refresh operations. The tokens are then returned to the client for use in subsequent authenticated requests.

The operation also checks whether the member account has been banned by examining the discussion_board_ban_record_of_members table. If a ban record exists and is active, the login attempt is rejected with a 403 Forbidden response, preventing banned users from accessing the platform.

The response includes both access and refresh tokens following the IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized structure, enabling immediate authenticated access to member features.

requestBody.description: Login credentials including email and password

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens for the logged-in member

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation refreshes the authentication tokens for an existing member session. The implementation must:

1. Validate the provided refresh token against the discussion_board_member_sessions table
2. Verify the refresh token is valid, not expired, and belongs to an active member
3. Check that the associated member account exists and is not banned
4. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens
5. Update the session record in discussion_board_member_sessions with the new tokens and timestamps
6. Return the new tokens in the IAuthorized response

Error handling:
- Return 401 Unauthorized if refresh token is invalid, expired, or not found
- Return 403 Forbidden if member account is banned
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database or token generation failures
operations.description:
This API operation allows members to obtain new authentication tokens without requiring re-authentication with credentials. The token refresh mechanism is essential for maintaining long-lived sessions while keeping access tokens short-lived for security purposes.

The operation validates the provided refresh token against the discussion_board_member_sessions table to ensure it is valid, not expired, and associated with an active member account. If the refresh token is valid, the system generates new JWT access and refresh tokens and updates the session record with the new tokens and current timestamp.

This approach provides several security benefits: access tokens can be kept short-lived to minimize the window of opportunity for token theft, while refresh tokens enable seamless session continuation without requiring users to re-enter credentials. The refresh token validation also includes checks for account ban status to ensure banned users cannot continue their sessions.

The response includes both new access and refresh tokens following the IDiscussionBoardMember.IAuthorized structure.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authentication tokens

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens for the member session

This operation creates a new administrator record in the discussion_board_administrators table with the provided email, hashed password, and optional display name and bio. The email must be unique across all administrator accounts as enforced by the unique constraint on the email column. Upon successful registration, the administrator is assigned a 'regular' grade by default and can immediately log in to access administrative features.

The password is hashed using a secure algorithm before storage in the password_hash column. The created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically set to record the account creation time. The administrator starts with no active sessions until they log in.

This operation is public and does not require authentication, allowing new administrators to register themselves. After registration, the administrator should use the login operation to obtain JWT tokens for authenticated access to protected resources.
operations.specification: Create a new record in discussion_board_administrators table with email, password_hash (hashed), display_name, bio, grade='regular', created_at, and updated_at fields. Validate email uniqueness before insertion. Hash the password using bcrypt or similar secure algorithm. Return authorization tokens (access and refresh) in the response. Set authorizationType to 'join' for proper authentication handling.

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Authenticate an administrator with email and password credentials. This operation validates the provided credentials against the discussion_board_administrators table by comparing the hashed password with the stored password_hash. Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created in the discussion_board_administrator_sessions table with access and refresh token hashes.

The session includes connection metadata (IP address, href, referrer) for security auditing. The access token expires after 15 minutes and the refresh token expires after 7 days, as configured in the access_token_expires_at and refresh_token_expires_at fields. Only one active session is allowed per administrator, enforced by the unique constraint on discussion_board_administrator_id.

This operation is public and does not require prior authentication. The returned tokens enable the administrator to access protected administrative resources and manage content, users, and system settings.
operations.specification: Validate email and password against discussion_board_administrators table. Hash the provided password and compare with stored password_hash. If valid, create or update a session record in discussion_board_administrator_sessions with token hashes, connection metadata, and expiration timestamps. Return JWT tokens (access and refresh) in the response. Set authorizationType to 'login' for proper authentication handling.

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens for the authenticated administrator

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Refresh the access token using a valid refresh token. This operation validates the refresh token against the discussion_board_administrator_sessions table by comparing the token hash with the stored refresh_token_hash. If valid and not expired, a new access token is generated and the session's access_token_expires_at timestamp is updated.

The refresh token itself remains valid until its expiration time (typically 7 days from initial login). This allows administrators to maintain continuous access without re-entering credentials. The operation also validates that the session has not been terminated (expired_at is null).

This operation is public but requires a valid refresh token. It enables seamless token renewal for administrators who have an active session, preventing authentication interruptions during extended administrative work sessions.
operations.specification: Validate the refresh token by comparing its hash with refresh_token_hash in discussion_board_administrator_sessions. Verify the session is active (expired_at is null) and refresh token is not expired. Generate a new access token and update access_token_expires_at. Return the new access token in the response. Set authorizationType to 'refresh' for proper authentication handling.

responseBody.description: New authorization tokens for the administrator

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query session data from three separate tables: discussion_board_member_sessions, discussion_board_administrator_sessions, and discussion_board_guest_sessions.

Apply filtering based on request parameters:
- Filter by session status (active if expired_at is null, expired otherwise)
- Filter by actor type (member, administrator, guest)
- Filter by actor ID (specific user session lookup)
- Filter by date range on created_at and/or expired_at fields
- Filter by IP address for security investigations

Apply sorting on created_at (default descending) or expired_at.

Apply cursor-based pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100).

Transform results into unified session summary format with actor_type discriminator field.

Include session statistics in response (total active sessions, total expired sessions).

Authorization: Require administrator role (regular or super admin) to access session data.

Performance: Use indexed queries on discussion_board_member_id, discussion_board_administrator_id, discussion_board_guest_id, created_at, and expired_at fields.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of authentication sessions across all actor types in the discussion board system.

This operation provides comprehensive session visibility for administrative purposes, enabling security auditing, user activity monitoring, and troubleshooting. It aggregates session data from member, administrator, and guest session tables into a unified view.

The operation supports advanced filtering capabilities including session status (active or expired), actor type (member, administrator, or guest), specific actor identification, date range filtering on session creation and expiration times, and IP address filtering for security investigations. Results can be sorted by creation time or expiration time.

Security considerations: This operation requires administrator privileges (either regular or super administrator) as it exposes sensitive authentication session information including IP addresses, connection metadata, and temporal data. The session data is used for security auditing, abuse detection, and compliance monitoring as specified in the observability requirements.

Related operations include individual session retrieval by ID (GET /sessions/{sessionId}), session termination (DELETE /sessions/{sessionId}), and actor-specific session queries. This operation should be used in conjunction with user management APIs for comprehensive account administration.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for session listing

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries with filtering results

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a specific session record by UUID from the appropriate session table based on session type.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the sessionId UUID format
2. Query discussion_board_member_sessions, discussion_board_administrator_sessions, and discussion_board_guest_sessions tables to find the matching session
3. Join with the corresponding user table (discussion_board_members, discussion_board_administrators, or discussion_board_guests) to include user information
4. Return session details including: id, user_id, user_type, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, is_active
5. If session not found, return 404 Not Found
6. Apply authorization check: only authenticated administrators can access this endpoint
7. Include token hash information only for administrator sessions (access_token_hash, refresh_token_hash, token expiration times)

Security considerations:
- Require administrator authentication
- Log access attempts for audit trail
- Mask sensitive information (token hashes should not be returned in plaintext)
- Validate session exists before returning data
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific user session by session identifier.

This operation provides comprehensive session details including connection metadata, temporal boundaries, and associated user information. It is designed for administrative monitoring, security auditing, and session management purposes.

The session data includes the IP address from which the session was created, the URL entry point (href), referrer information, session creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. For administrator sessions, additional token metadata is available including access token and refresh token expiration times.

Authorization: This endpoint requires administrator authentication. Regular members and guests cannot access session information for security and privacy reasons. Only authenticated administrators can retrieve session details to support security monitoring and user management tasks.

Related operations: Use PATCH /sessions to list and filter sessions with pagination. Use DELETE /sessions/{sessionId} to terminate an active session. Session data is append-only and never modified after creation.

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_members table with pagination and filtering capabilities.

1. Apply search filters:
   - Partial text matching on display_name using trigram similarity (GIN index)
   - Email domain or exact matching
   - Account status filtering (banned boolean)
   - Date range filtering on created_at

2. Apply sorting:
   - Default: created_at descending (newest first)
   - Supported: created_at, updated_at, display_name (ascending/descending)

3. Apply pagination:
   - Cursor-based or offset-based pagination
   - Configurable page size with reasonable defaults (e.g., 20 items)
   - Return pagination metadata (total count, has more)

4. Authorization checks:
   - Members: can query other members' public profiles
   - Administrators: can query all members including banned status
   - Exclude deleted members (deleted_at is not null) unless admin with explicit flag

5. Response transformation:
   - Return ISummary variant with essential fields only
   - Exclude password_hash for security
   - Include derived fields: article count, comment count (via relation counts)

6. Error handling:
   - Invalid sort field: return 400 Bad Request
   - Invalid pagination parameters: return 400 Bad Request
   - Unauthorized access: return 403 Forbidden
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of registered member accounts from the discussion board platform.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for browsing member profiles. Members can search for other users by display name or email, filter by account status, and sort results by various criteria. The response includes essential profile information optimized for list displays and search results.

Search functionality supports partial text matching on display names using trigram similarity for flexible user discovery. Email filtering allows exact matching or domain-based searches. Account status filtering enables viewing only active members or including banned accounts (administrator access required).

Pagination is supported with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Results can be ordered by registration date, last update time, or display name in ascending or descending order. The default sorting is by registration date with newest members first.

Security considerations: Regular members can only view public profile information of other users. Administrators have access to additional fields including ban status and can view all members regardless of account state. Password hashes and sensitive authentication data are never included in responses.

Related operations: Use GET /members/{memberId} to retrieve detailed information about a specific member, including their articles and comments. Use PUT /members/{memberId} to update member profile information (own profile only).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member profile summaries with pagination metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed profile information for a specific discussion board member by their unique identifier.

This operation returns comprehensive member profile data including display name, biographical information, account status, and timestamps. The member's email address and password hash are never exposed in the response for security reasons.

Authorization rules: Members can view their own complete profile and other members' public profiles. Administrators have access to view all member profiles including sensitive status information such as banned status. Guest users cannot access member profiles.

The operation supports viewing profiles for the purpose of understanding article authorship, comment attribution, and community member information. When a member is banned, their profile remains viewable but their ability to log in and create new content is restricted.

Related operations include viewing articles written by a member, viewing comments written by a member, and for administrators, managing member accounts through ban/unban operations.

The display name is shown on articles, comments, and profile pages as the member's public identity. The bio text is optional and provides additional information about the member.

Only authenticated members can access this endpoint. The member's identity is determined from the authentication session or token. Banned members are prevented from updating their profile information.

The display name and bio fields are both optional. Members can set them to empty strings or null values. Changes to the profile are reflected immediately across all the member's content including articles and comments.

Related operations include viewing the profile (GET /profile), viewing articles written by a member, and viewing comments written by a member.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of password reset requests across all user accounts for security auditing purposes.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive visibility into password reset activity across the discussion board platform. It combines password reset records from both member and administrator accounts, enabling security teams to monitor reset patterns, investigate suspicious activity, and maintain audit compliance.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering capabilities including user type filtering (members vs administrators), status filtering (used vs unused tokens), date range queries, and searches by user identifiers, email addresses, IP addresses, or user agent strings. This allows administrators to quickly locate specific reset requests or identify anomalous patterns.

Access to this operation is restricted to authenticated administrators only (both regular and super administrators) due to the sensitive nature of security audit data. All access to this endpoint is logged for accountability and security monitoring purposes.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with user management operations to investigate account security incidents, verify legitimate password reset requests, or respond to security alerts about unusual reset activity.

Implementation steps:

2. Query discussion_board_member_password_resets table first using the id field
3. If not found, query discussion_board_administrator_password_resets table
4. Verify the requesting user has appropriate authorization (admin or token owner)
5. Return the password reset record with associated user information
6. Include token status: unused (used_at is null), expired (current time > expired_at), or used (used_at is set)
7. Join with member or administrator table to include user email and display name
8. Handle case where token record doesn't exist - return 404
9. Handle unauthorized access - return 403

- Only administrators should be able to view all password reset records
- Regular members can only view their own password reset tokens
- Token values should be masked or partially hidden in responses for security
- Log all access attempts to password reset records for audit trail
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific password reset token by its unique identifier.

This operation returns comprehensive details about a password reset token, including its current status (unused, used, or expired), creation timestamp, expiration time, and the associated user account information. The password reset token is a time-limited, single-use credential generated when a user requests to reset their password without knowing their current credentials.

The response includes the token's usage state, indicating whether it has been redeemed for a password change, when it expires, and audit information such as the user agent and IP address from the original reset request. This information is valuable for administrators monitoring account security activities and for users verifying their password reset requests.

Access to this operation requires appropriate authentication. Administrators can view any password reset record for security auditing purposes, while regular members can only access their own password reset tokens. This restriction ensures that sensitive authentication recovery information remains protected from unauthorized access.

Related operations include the password reset request creation endpoint and the password update endpoint that consumes the token to complete the reset process.

operations.name: index

3. Apply search filter on email and display_name fields using LIKE or full-text search
4. Apply sorting based on request parameters (default: created_at DESC)
5. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach

**Authorization**:
- Require administrator authentication (actor kind: admin)
- Verify the requesting user is an active administrator (not banned)
- Super administrators can view all administrators
- Regular administrators can view all administrators

**Response Construction**:
- Return paginated wrapper with metadata (total count, page size, cursor)
- Include administrator summary fields: id, email, display_name, grade, created_at
- Exclude sensitive fields: password_hash, deleted_at
- Optionally include bio if not null

**Edge Cases**:
- Handle empty result sets with zero total count
- Handle pagination beyond available records
- Handle invalid grade filter values (return error or ignore)
- Handle very large result sets with appropriate page size limits
operations.description:

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for administrator management. Administrators can search by email address or display name, filter by administrator grade (regular or super), and sort results by various criteria including creation date, email, or display name.

The endpoint supports pagination to efficiently handle large administrator populations. Each response includes pagination metadata such as total count, current page size, and cursor information for navigating through result sets.

**Security Considerations**:

This operation requires administrator authentication. Only users with administrator privileges (either regular or super administrator grade) can access this endpoint. The operation excludes sensitive fields such as password hashes from the response.

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /administrators/{administratorId}` - Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator
- `POST /administrators` - Create a new administrator account (typically handled through admin request approval workflow)
- `PUT /administrators/{administratorId}` - Update administrator information
- `DELETE /administrators/{administratorId}` - Remove an administrator account

**Database Entity**:

This operation queries the `discussion_board_administrators` table, which stores administrator accounts with email and password authentication credentials, display names, biographical information, and grade levels (regular or super).

The response includes both regular administrators and super administrators, with the grade field indicating the privilege level.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated administrators only. Regular administrators can view other administrators' profiles for collaboration purposes, while super administrators have full visibility into all administrator accounts for governance and oversight responsibilities.

- Search by section description using partial text matching
- Filter results to show only active sections (excludes soft-deleted sections)

- `POST /sections` creates a new section (administrator only)

operations.name: create

Create a new section in the discussion_board_sections table.

1. Validate administrator authorization - only users with administrator role can create sections.

2. Validate request body:
   - name: Required, non-empty string
   - description: Optional string
   - Check name uniqueness against existing active sections (deleted_at IS NULL)

3. Insert new record into discussion_board_sections:
   - id: Generate UUID
   - name: From request
   - description: From request (nullable)

operations.description:
Create a new section to organize articles by topic within the discussion board.

This operation allows administrators to create organizational containers for grouping related articles. Each section serves as a topic category (e.g., Politics, Economy, Current Affairs) that helps users browse and discover content by subject matter.

**Authorization**: Only users with administrator privileges can create sections. This restriction ensures that the organizational structure of the discussion board is maintained by trusted users with elevated permissions.

**Required Fields**:
- **name**: A unique, human-readable identifier for the section. This name must be distinct from all other active sections in the system. The name is used for display purposes and section navigation.
- **description**: An optional text field that explains the section's purpose, scope, and content guidelines. While not required, providing a clear description helps users understand what type of articles belong in each section.

**Business Rules**:
- Section names must be unique across the entire discussion board to prevent confusion and duplicate categorization.
- Sections are immediately available for article assignment after creation.
- Created sections are tracked with timestamps for audit purposes.
- Sections support soft deletion, allowing administrators to remove sections while preserving historical data.

**Related Operations**:
- `PATCH /sections`: List all available sections with filtering and pagination
- `GET /sections/{sectionId}`: Retrieve detailed information about a specific section
- `PUT /sections/{sectionId}`: Update an existing section's name and description
- `DELETE /sections/{sectionId}`: Soft delete a section (admin only)

requestBody.description: Section creation information including name and optional description

responseBody.description: Created section with all fields including generated identifiers and timestamps

operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an existing section in the discussion_board_sections table.

1. Validate the sectionId path parameter is a valid UUID.
2. Verify the requesting user has administrator privileges (regular or super administrator).
3. Query the discussion_board_sections table for the section by id.
4. If section does not exist, return 404 Not Found.
5. If section is soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404 Not Found.
6. Validate the request body:
   - If name is provided, check it's not empty and doesn't conflict with another active section's name.
   - If description is provided, accept null to clear the description.
7. Update the section record with provided fields:
   - name: Update if provided (must be unique among active sections).
   - description: Update if provided (nullable).
   - updated_at: Set to current timestamp.
8. Do not modify created_at or deleted_at fields.
9. Create a snapshot in discussion_board_section_snapshots before the update for audit trail.
10. Return the updated section entity with all current values.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized if user is not authenticated.
- 403 Forbidden if user is not an administrator.
- 404 Not Found if section doesn't exist or is soft deleted.
- 409 Conflict if name conflicts with another active section.
- 400 Bad Request if validation fails (empty name, etc.).
operations.description:
Update an existing section's properties in the discussion board.

This operation allows administrators to modify the name and description of an existing section. Sections serve as organizational containers for grouping related articles by topic, and this endpoint provides the ability to update section metadata as topics evolve or need clarification.

Only authenticated administrators (both regular and super administrators) have permission to update sections. This restriction ensures that the organizational structure of the discussion board remains controlled and consistent. Regular users and guests can only view sections but cannot modify them.

The section is identified by its unique UUID in the path parameter. The request body contains the fields to update: name (the unique identifier for the section) and description (optional explanatory text about the section's purpose and scope). The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect the modification time.

Before updating, the system validates that any new name does not conflict with existing active sections to maintain uniqueness. If the section has been soft deleted, the update is rejected. A snapshot of the section's previous state is created in the discussion_board_section_snapshots table for audit trail purposes, preserving the history of all modifications.

Related operations include GET /sections/{sectionId} to retrieve a specific section, PATCH /sections to list all sections with filtering, POST /sections to create a new section, and DELETE /sections/{sectionId} to soft delete a section.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the section to update

requestBody.description: Updated section properties

responseBody.description: Updated section entity

operations.description:
Delete a discussion board section by its unique identifier. This operation permanently removes the section from the platform, making it inaccessible to all users.

This administrative operation is restricted to administrator accounts only. Regular members and guests cannot delete sections. The operation implements soft deletion, marking the section as deleted in the database while preserving the record for audit purposes.

Before deletion can proceed, the system validates that the section contains no articles. If articles exist in the section, the deletion request is rejected and the administrator must first reassign or remove all articles. This ensures referential integrity and prevents orphaned articles.

The operation updates the deleted_at timestamp to record when the section was removed. The section name becomes available for future use, but the original section record remains in the database for historical tracking and audit trail purposes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting user has administrator privileges by checking their session and role in discussion_board_administrators table.

Retrieve the section record from discussion_board_sections using the provided sectionId. Verify the section exists and is not already soft deleted.

Query discussion_board_articles to check if any articles belong to this section (where section_id matches and deleted_at is null). If articles exist, reject the deletion with a 409 Conflict response.

If the section is empty, perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp. Do not permanently remove the record from the database.

Return the deleted section details including the new deleted_at timestamp to confirm successful deletion.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the section to delete

prerequisites.description: Section must be created before it can be deleted. The sectionId parameter references an existing section record.

- Search on name and description fields
- Pagination parameters (page, pageSize)
- Sorting by created_at (default descending for recent snapshots first)

Join with discussion_board_sections to validate section existence.

Return paginated results with snapshot summaries containing:
- Snapshot ID, name, description, section_created_at, section_updated_at, created_at

Handle edge cases:
- Return empty array if section has no snapshots
- Return 404 if section ID doesn't exist
- Validate date ranges for proper ordering

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of historical section snapshots for audit and revision tracking purposes.

This operation provides access to point-in-time snapshots that capture the complete state of a section at the moment of modification. Each snapshot preserves the section's name, description, and timestamps, enabling administrators to track section configuration changes over time for compliance and audit requirements.

The snapshots are immutable records that maintain an accurate audit trail of all section modifications. This is particularly useful for understanding the evolution of section configurations, investigating past changes, and maintaining compliance with data retention policies.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrators only, as it provides sensitive audit information about section modification history. The snapshots reference the discussion_board_sections table and capture denormalized section properties to preserve exact historical state independent of current section data.

Related operations include retrieving the current section state via GET /sections/{sectionId} and viewing section articles via GET /sections/{sectionId}/articles.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific section snapshot by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete state of a section at a specific point in time, captured for audit trail and revision history purposes. Section snapshots are immutable records that preserve the exact state of a section when modifications occurred, enabling version control and historical analysis.

The snapshot includes the section's name, description, and timestamps for when the section was originally created, when it was last modified before the snapshot was taken, and when the snapshot itself was created. This temporal information allows administrators to track the evolution of section configurations over time.

Access to section snapshots is available to all authenticated users, supporting transparency and accountability in section management. The snapshot data is read-only and cannot be modified through this or any other API operation.

This operation is typically used after retrieving a list of snapshots for a section to view the detailed state of a specific historical version. Related operations include listing all snapshots for a section and retrieving the current section state.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_section_snapshots table for a single record matching both the section ID and snapshot ID.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate that both sectionId and snapshotId are valid UUIDs
2. Execute a database query to find the snapshot record where id = snapshotId AND discussion_board_sections_id = sectionId
3. Verify the snapshot exists and belongs to the specified section (security check)
4. Return the snapshot data including all fields: id, name, description, section_created_at, section_updated_at, created_at
5. If no matching snapshot is found, return 404 Not Found
6. If the snapshot exists but does not belong to the specified section, return 404 Not Found (prevents information leakage)

The query should use a composite condition on both the primary key (id) and foreign key (discussion_board_sections_id) to ensure the snapshot belongs to the specified section.

No authentication is required for this operation as section snapshots are publicly accessible for transparency.

responseBody.description: Section snapshot with complete historical state

operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_articles table with pagination and filtering.

**Query Construction**:
1. Base query selects active articles (deleted_at IS NULL) for non-admin users
2. For administrators, include option to show soft-deleted articles via request parameter
3. Apply section filter: JOIN discussion_board_sections, filter by section_id if provided
4. Apply tag filter: JOIN discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags, filter by tag IDs (AND logic - must have all specified tags)
5. Apply author filter: JOIN discussion_board_members, filter by member_id if provided
6. Apply search filter: Use trigram similarity on title and content fields for partial matching
7. Apply date range filter: Filter by created_at between provided dates
8. Apply sorting: Default ORDER BY created_at DESC, support title ASC/DESC, updated_at ASC/DESC
9. Apply pagination: Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size

**Business Rules**:
- Exclude soft-deleted articles unless user is administrator and explicitly requests them
- Validate section_id references existing active section
- Validate tag_ids reference existing tags
- Validate author_id references existing member
- Search query minimum 2 characters, maximum 100 characters
- Page size limited to 100 maximum, default 20

**Performance Considerations**:
- Use indexed fields: discussion_board_section_id, created_at, deleted_at
- Leverage GIN trigram indexes on title and content for search
- Use composite index on (discussion_board_section_id, created_at) for section filtering
- Cache tag lookups for repeated queries

**Error Handling**:
- Return 400 for invalid search parameters (non-existent section, tag, author)
- Return 400 for page size exceeding maximum
- Return empty array for no matching results (not an error)
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of articles from the discussion board platform.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for browsing articles. Users can filter articles by section, tags, author, creation date range, and perform full-text search on article titles and content. The response includes article summary information optimized for list displays, with pagination metadata for navigating large result sets.

**Filtering Capabilities**:

- **Section Filtering**: Filter articles by specific section ID to browse content within a particular topic category
- **Tag Filtering**: Filter by one or more tags (AND logic - articles must have all specified tags)
- **Author Filtering**: Filter articles by specific member ID to view content from a particular user
- **Text Search**: Full-text search across article titles and content using trigram similarity for partial matching
- **Date Range Filtering**: Filter articles by creation date range to find recent or historical content

**Sorting Options**:

- By creation date (newest or oldest first) - default is newest first
- By title alphabetically (ascending or descending)
- By last update date (most or least recently updated)

**Access Control**:

- **Guest users**: Can view all active articles (not soft-deleted) with public access
- **Member users**: Can view all active articles, with ability to filter by their own articles
- **Administrator users**: Can view all articles including soft-deleted ones when explicitly requested, with full filtering capabilities

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`: Retrieve detailed information for a specific article
- `POST /discussionBoard/articles`: Create a new article (requires member authentication)
- `PUT /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`: Update an existing article (requires ownership or admin access)
- `DELETE /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`: Delete an article (requires ownership or admin access)
- `PATCH /discussionBoard/sections`: List available sections for filtering
- `PATCH /discussionBoard/tags`: List available tags for filtering

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for article listing

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summaries with pagination metadata

Authorization:

- No write permissions required

Return the article with full content, section details, author information, tags array, and comment count.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single article by its unique identifier from the discussion board platform.

This operation fetches the complete article content including title, full text, author information, section details, associated tags, and comment count. The article must exist and not be soft-deleted to be retrievable. All users including guests can view articles, supporting the platform's open browsing model.

The response includes the article's creation and update timestamps, the section to which it belongs, the author's display name and bio, all tags assigned to the article, and the total count of comments. Articles are organized by sections for categorization, and each article must belong to exactly one active section.

Related operations include listing articles in a section (PATCH /sections/{sectionId}/articles), searching articles (PATCH /articles), viewing article comments (GET /articles/{articleId}/comments), and retrieving section information (GET /sections/{sectionId}).

operations.description:
Create a new article in a discussion board section.

This operation allows authenticated members to create articles with title, content, section assignment, and optional tags. Every article must be assigned to exactly one active section for organizational categorization. The article is automatically associated with the authenticated member's account and creation session for ownership tracking and audit purposes.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated members can create articles. Guests and banned users are rejected. The system validates that the member's account is active and not banned before allowing article creation. The authenticated member's ID and session ID are automatically captured from the request context.

Section validation: The specified section must exist and be active (not soft-deleted). If the section has been deleted by an administrator, the article creation is rejected with an error. The system ensures every article belongs to exactly one section as required by business rules.

Tag assignment: Articles can have multiple free-text tags assigned for categorization and filtering. Tags are created dynamically if they don't already exist in the system. The many-to-many relationship between articles and tags is managed through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

Related operations: After creation, use GET /articles/{articleId} to retrieve the full article details. Use PATCH /articles to search and list articles with filtering. Use PUT /articles/{articleId} to edit the article. Use DELETE /articles/{articleId} to delete the article.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Service layer implementation for article creation:

1. Authentication: Extract member ID and session ID from the authenticated request context. Verify the member exists and is not banned (banned = false) and not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).

2. Section validation: Query discussion_board_sections by the provided sectionId. Verify the section exists and is active (deleted_at is null). If section is deleted or doesn't exist, throw a validation error.

3. Article creation: Insert a new record into discussion_board_articles with:
   - id: Generate new UUID
   - discussion_board_section_id: From request body
   - discussion_board_member_id: From authenticated context
   - discussion_board_member_session_id: From authenticated context
   - title: From request body (validate not empty)
   - content: From request body (validate not empty)
   - created_at: Current timestamp
   - updated_at: Current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null

4. Tag processing: For each tag name in the request:
   - Query discussion_board_tags by name (case-sensitive, exact match)
   - If tag exists, use its ID
   - If tag doesn't exist, insert new record into discussion_board_tags with generated UUID, name, and current timestamp
   - Insert record into discussion_board_article_tags linking article ID and tag ID with current created_at timestamp

5. Return the created article with full details including author display name and assigned tags.

Error handling:
- Return 401 if not authenticated
- Return 403 if member is banned
- Return 404 if section doesn't exist or is deleted
- Return 400 if title or content is empty

responseBody.description: Created article with full details including author and tags

requestBody.description: Article creation data including title, content, section, and optional tags

prerequisites.description: Section must exist and be active before an article can be assigned to it

operations.name: update

Update an existing article's title, content, and/or section assignment.

Authorization:
- Verify authenticated user is either the article's author (discussion_board_member_id matches current user) OR has administrator role
- Reject with 403 Forbidden if unauthorized

Validation:
- Verify article exists by articleId
- Verify article is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL)
- If sectionId provided in request, verify section exists and is not deleted
- Validate title is non-empty string
- Validate content is non-empty string
- If updating section, ensure target section is active (deleted_at is NULL)

Business Logic:
- Update title field if provided in request
- Update content field if provided in request
- Update discussion_board_section_id if sectionId provided in request
- Update updated_at timestamp to current time
- Preserve discussion_board_member_id (author cannot change)
- Preserve created_at timestamp
- Preserve deleted_at value (this is not a restore operation)

Database Operations:
- Single UPDATE query on discussion_board_articles table
- SET title = ?, content = ?, discussion_board_section_id = ?, updated_at = ?
- WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
- Use transaction if section change is involved to ensure referential integrity

Error Handling:
- 404 Not Found: article does not exist or is soft-deleted
- 403 Forbidden: user is not article author and not administrator
- 400 Bad Request: invalid title, content, or sectionId
- 400 Bad Request: target section does not exist or is deleted
operations.description:
Update an existing article's title, content, and section assignment.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify the content of articles they own. Only the article's original author or an administrator can perform updates. Regular members can only update articles they created, while administrators have elevated permissions to modify any article for content moderation purposes. This dual authorization model ensures content integrity while enabling necessary editorial oversight.

The operation supports partial updates - clients can provide only the fields they wish to change while leaving others unchanged. Article updates are restricted to active articles only; soft-deleted articles cannot be updated through this endpoint. The soft-delete status (deleted_at field) is preserved and cannot be modified, ensuring that this operation does not restore deleted content.

Section reassignment is supported, allowing articles to be moved between sections. When changing an article's section, the target section must exist and be active (not deleted). This enables administrators to reorganize content as section structures evolve over time.

The operation preserves critical audit information including the original author, creation timestamp, and soft-delete status. The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect the modification time, maintaining an accurate audit trail for content changes. This aligns with the discussion_board_articles table schema which tracks both created_at and updated_at for revision history.

operations.description:
Delete an article from the discussion board platform.

This operation permanently removes an article from all public views and listings. When an article is deleted, the system also cascades deletion to all associated comments and attachments to maintain data integrity and prevent orphaned records.

Authorization is enforced based on user roles and ownership:

- **Article Authors**: Registered members can delete articles they created. The system verifies that the requesting user's member ID matches the article's author ID before allowing deletion.
- **Administrators**: Administrators have elevated permissions to delete any article regardless of authorship. This enables content moderation and enforcement of community guidelines.
- **Banned Users**: Users with banned accounts cannot perform deletion operations, even on their own articles.

The deletion process uses soft deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp. This preserves the article record in the database for audit purposes while removing it from active article listings, search results, and section views. Soft deletion ensures historical data integrity and supports potential restoration workflows.

Related operations:

- `PATCH /articles` - List and search articles with filters
- `GET /articles/{articleId}` - Retrieve a specific article by ID
- `PUT /articles/{articleId}` - Update an existing article
- `POST /articles` - Create a new article

Validate the articleId parameter as a UUID format string.

Retrieve the article record from discussion_board_articles table using the articleId.

Verify authorization:
1. Check if the requesting user is an administrator - if yes, allow deletion
2. If not administrator, verify the requesting user's member ID matches the article's discussion_board_member_id
3. Check if the requesting user's account is banned - reject if banned

Perform soft deletion:
1. Set deleted_at timestamp to current time on the article record
2. Cascade soft delete to all comments in discussion_board_comments where discussion_board_article_id matches
3. Cascade delete to all attachments associated with the article
4. Cascade delete to all article views in discussion_board_article_views
5. Cascade delete to all tag assignments in discussion_board_article_tags

Return 204 No Content status on successful deletion.

Handle edge cases:
- Return 404 Not Found if article does not exist
- Return 403 Forbidden if user lacks authorization
- Return 403 Forbidden if user account is banned
- Return 400 Bad Request if articleId is invalid UUID format

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of article snapshots for a specific article.

This operation provides access to the revision history of an article, showing all point-in-time snapshots captured when the article was modified. Each snapshot preserves the complete state of the article at a specific moment, including title, content, section assignment, and author information.

Snapshots are immutable historical records created automatically whenever an article is modified. They enable audit trails, content accountability, and potential content restoration. The snapshots are ordered chronologically with the most recent modifications appearing first.

Access to article snapshots requires the article to exist and be active. Articles that have been soft-deleted cannot have their snapshots accessed through this endpoint. The operation supports filtering by date range and title text, enabling users to find specific modifications within the article's history.

This endpoint is read-only as snapshots are system-generated audit records that cannot be modified or deleted by users. The snapshot data includes author display names and section names for better context when reviewing the article's modification history.

Related operations:
- `GET /articles/{articleId}` retrieves the current state of the article
- `PUT /articles/{articleId}` updates the article, which creates a new snapshot

Snapshots enable users and administrators to:
- Track all modifications made to articles over time
- View previous versions of article content for comparison
- Maintain accountability records for compliance and auditing
- Understand the evolution of article content through revision history

Each snapshot contains the article's title, full content text, author information (display name), section assignment, and the exact timestamp when the snapshot was created. The snapshot also references the authentication session used when the modification occurred for complete audit trail traceability.

Access Control:
- Guests can view snapshots of public articles
- Members can view snapshots of their own articles and all public articles
- Administrators can view all article snapshots regardless of ownership or visibility

Related Operations:
- `PATCH /articles/{articleId}/snapshots` - List all snapshots for a specific article
- `GET /articles/{articleId}` - View the current version of an article
- `GET /sections/{sectionId}/articles` - Browse articles within a section
