operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new article snapshot by capturing the current state of the target article.

1. Validate that the article exists and is accessible to the requesting user
2. Verify the article has not been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
3. Capture the current article state: title, content, section_id, member_id
4. Create a new record in discussion_board_article_snapshots table with:
   - discussion_board_article_id: reference to the source article
   - discussion_board_member_id: current article author
   - discussion_board_section_id: current section assignment
   - discussion_board_member_session_id: current authentication session
   - title: current article title
   - content: current article content
   - created_at: current timestamp
5. Return the created snapshot with all fields including generated id
6. Ensure transactional consistency - snapshot creation should not fail partially

Authorization: Only administrators or the article author should be able to create snapshots manually. System automatically creates snapshots on article modifications.

Edge cases:
- Article not found: return 404
- Article is deleted: return 400 with error message
- User not authorized: return 403
- Section no longer exists: still create snapshot but mark section reference as historical
operations.description:
Create a point-in-time snapshot of an article for audit trail and revision history purposes.

This operation captures the complete state of an article at the current moment, preserving the title, content, section assignment, and author information as an immutable historical record. Article snapshots enable organizations to maintain compliance audit trails, track content modifications over time, and potentially restore previous versions of articles.

The snapshot operation is typically used by administrators for compliance purposes or triggered automatically when articles are modified. Each snapshot is append-only and never modified or deleted after creation, ensuring the integrity of the audit trail.

Related operations include retrieving article snapshots via GET /articles/{articleId}/snapshots to view the revision history, and viewing individual snapshot details via GET /articles/{articleId}/snapshots/{snapshotId}.

Authorization requires the user to be either the article author or an administrator with appropriate permissions to access audit trail functionality.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: UUID of the article to create a snapshot for

responseBody.description: Created article snapshot with full details

prerequisites.description: Article must exist before a snapshot can be created for it

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of view events for a specific article.

This operation provides analytics data about article engagement by returning all view events for the specified article. Each view event records when an article was accessed, whether by an authenticated member or a guest user. The data supports engagement analytics, popular content identification, and user reading history features.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering capabilities including date range queries to analyze viewing patterns over time, member-specific filtering to track individual user reading history, and session-based filtering for detailed access tracking. Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page sizes.

Access to this endpoint is available to authenticated members for viewing their own reading history and to administrators for platform-wide analytics. Guest users cannot access detailed view analytics. The article must exist and not be soft-deleted for view data to be returned.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} for retrieving the full article content, and PATCH /articles for listing articles within a section. View analytics data is automatically generated when articles are accessed and cannot be manually created or modified.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_article_views table with filtering by discussion_board_article_id (from path parameter).

Apply pagination from request body (page, pageSize) with cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

Support filtering by:
- Date range on viewed_at field for temporal analysis
- discussion_board_member_id for member-specific view history
- discussion_board_member_session_id for session-based tracking

Join with discussion_board_members to include member display names when views are from authenticated users.

Return view summaries containing: view id, viewed_at timestamp, member display name (or null for guests), and session context.

Sort by viewed_at descending (newest first) by default, support ascending order via request body.

Validate that the article exists and is not soft-deleted before returning view data.

Handle empty result sets when no views exist for the article.

Apply rate limiting to prevent abuse of analytics endpoints.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article view summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for view events

operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_article_views table to retrieve a single view record by view ID.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate that both articleId and viewId are valid UUIDs
2. Query discussion_board_article_views WHERE id = viewId AND discussion_board_article_id = articleId
3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found
4. Join with discussion_board_articles to verify the article exists and is not soft-deleted
5. Optionally join with discussion_board_members to include viewer information if discussion_board_member_id is not null
6. Return the view record with all fields: id, article_id, member_id, member_session_id, viewed_at
7. Handle case where view belongs to different article than specified in path (return 404)

Authorization:
- Guest users: Can view their own anonymous view records
- Members: Can view their own view records
- Administrators: Can view all view records for analytics purposes

Error handling:
- 404 if viewId doesn't exist
- 404 if viewId exists but doesn't belong to the specified articleId
- 403 if user tries to view another user's view record (unless admin)
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific article view event.

This operation returns complete information about a single article view record, including which article was viewed, by whom (if authenticated), the session context, and the exact timestamp of the view. Article views are automatically tracked by the system whenever users access articles, enabling engagement analytics, reading history, and popular content identification.

The view record contains the article identifier, optional member identifier (null for guest views), optional session identifier for tracking authentication context, and the viewed_at timestamp. This data is used for analytics dashboards showing article popularity, user reading history features, and engagement metrics.

Authorization depends on the viewer's role: guests can only access their own anonymous view records, members can access their own authenticated view records, and administrators have full access to all view records for platform analytics and monitoring purposes.

Related operations include listing all views for an article (PATCH /articles/{articleId}/views) for analytics purposes, and viewing article details (GET /articles/{articleId}) which may include view count statistics.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of comments belonging to a specific article.

This operation queries the discussion_board_comments table to return comments attached to the specified article. Comments are filtered to exclude soft-deleted records (where deleted_at IS NULL), ensuring only active comments are displayed. The results are returned in chronological order (oldest first) as required by the single-level comment structure.

Advanced search capabilities include content text filtering using trigram matching, author filtering by member ID, and date range queries on the created_at timestamp. The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and maintains sorting preferences across page navigation.

Authorization: All authenticated users can view comments on articles. Members can edit and delete only their own comments. Administrators have elevated permissions to delete any comment for content moderation purposes. Guests can also view comments without authentication.

Related operations: GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId} retrieves the full article. POST /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments creates a new comment. PUT /discussionBoard/comments/{commentId} updates an existing comment. DELETE /discussionBoard/comments/{commentId} soft-deletes a comment by setting deleted_at.

operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_comments table with the following logic:

1. Filter by discussion_board_article_id matching the articleId path parameter
2. Apply soft delete filter: deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted comments)
3. Apply search filters from request body:
   - Content text search using gin_trgm_ops index for partial matching
   - Author filtering by discussion_board_member_id
   - Date range filtering on created_at
4. Apply pagination: OFFSET and LIMIT based on page and pageSize
5. Apply sorting: default ORDER BY created_at ASC (chronological, oldest first)
6. Join with discussion_board_members to include author display name and profile information
7. Return paginated response with total count, pagination metadata, and comment summaries

Edge cases:
- Return empty paginated result if article has no comments
- Return 404 if articleId does not exist or article is soft-deleted
- Exclude soft-deleted comments from results
- Ensure proper authorization checking before returning results

Performance considerations:
- Use existing indexes: discussion_board_article_id + created_at
- Leverage gin_trgm_ops index for content text search
- Limit join complexity to only necessary fields for summary view

operations.name: at

Query the discussion_board_comments table for a single comment record matching both the articleId and commentId path parameters.

Verify the comment exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL). If deleted_at has a value, return 404 Not Found.

Validate authorization: the requesting user must be either the comment's author (matching discussion_board_member_id) or an administrator with elevated privileges.

Join with discussion_board_members to retrieve author information (display name, profile data).

Join with discussion_board_articles to verify the comment belongs to the specified article and that the article itself is not deleted.

Return the complete comment object including all fields: id, content, created_at, updated_at, and author details.

Handle edge cases: missing comment returns 404, deleted comment returns 404, unauthorized access returns 403 Forbidden.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific comment from an article by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a single comment, including the full text content, creation and modification timestamps, and the author's profile information. Comments are user-generated contributions that enable community discussion on articles.

Comments use soft deletion to preserve historical data. This endpoint will not return comments that have been deleted (marked with a deleted_at timestamp). Attempting to access a deleted comment will result in a 404 Not Found response.

Authorization is enforced at the comment level. Only the comment's author or administrators with elevated privileges can retrieve comment details. This protects user privacy while allowing content moderation by platform administrators.

The comment is retrieved within the context of its parent article. Both the article ID and comment ID are required in the path to ensure the comment belongs to the specified article and to provide proper resource scoping.

Related operations include listing all comments on an article (PATCH /articles/{articleId}/comments), creating a new comment (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments), updating a comment (PUT /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}), and deleting a comment (DELETE /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}).

Validate that the authenticated user is a registered member (not guest or banned).

Verify the article exists by querying discussion_board_articles where id = articleId and deleted_at IS NULL.

Validate that the article's section still exists (section should not be deleted).

Check that the authenticated member is not banned by verifying discussion_board_members banned status.

- discussion_board_article_id: from path parameter articleId
- discussion_board_member_id: from authenticated session
- content: from request body (validate non-empty, trim whitespace)
- created_at: current timestamp
- updated_at: current timestamp

Return the created comment with all fields including generated id and timestamps.

Handle errors: article not found, article deleted, user banned, user not authenticated, empty content.
operations.description:
Create a new comment on a discussion board article.

This operation allows registered members to post comments on articles as part of community discussions. Comments are stored in the discussion_board_comments table and are displayed in chronological order (oldest first) when viewing an article. Each comment is authored by a registered member and permanently associated with a specific article.

Security and validation: Only authenticated members can create comments. Guests and banned users are prevented from posting. The system validates that the target article exists, has not been deleted, and belongs to an active section. Comment content must be non-empty after trimming whitespace.

The comment structure is single-level with no nested replies or threaded discussions. All comments on an article appear as a flat, linear list. When an article is deleted, all its associated comments are automatically removed through cascading delete.

Related operations: Use GET /articles/{articleId}/comments to retrieve all comments on an article, PUT /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} to edit your own comment, and DELETE /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} to remove your own comment.

operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update a comment's content with authorization validation.

1. Parse path parameters: articleId (UUID) and commentId (UUID)
2. Authenticate the request and extract the actor (member or administrator)
3. Query discussion_board_comments table for the comment record:
   - WHERE id = commentId AND discussion_board_article_id = articleId
   - Ensure comment belongs to the specified article
   - Check deleted_at IS NULL (comment must be active)
4. Verify authorization:
   - If actor is member: verify discussion_board_member_id matches actor's ID
   - If actor is administrator: allow any comment update
   - Reject if neither condition is met (403 Forbidden)
5. Update the comment record:
   - Set content field from request body
   - Update updated_at to current timestamp
   - Do not modify created_at, discussion_board_article_id, or discussion_board_member_id
6. Return the updated comment with full details including author information

Error handling:
- 404 if comment not found or deleted
- 404 if article not found
- 403 if unauthorized (member trying to edit another's comment)
- 400 if content is empty or exceeds length limits
operations.description:
Update an existing comment's content on a discussion board article.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify the text content of a comment they have authored. Members can only edit their own comments, while administrators have the privilege to edit any comment regardless of authorship. The comment must be active (not deleted) and must belong to the specified article.

The update operation modifies only the content field and the updated_at timestamp. All other fields including the author identity, article association, and creation timestamp remain unchanged. This ensures audit trail integrity while allowing content corrections.

Comments are displayed in chronological order with oldest first, and the updated comment maintains its original position in the sequence. The author's display name and original creation time are preserved, with only the content text being replaced.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} for retrieving a single comment, DELETE /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} for removing a comment, and POST /articles/{articleId}/comments for creating new comments.

operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a comment from the discussion_board_comments table using soft deletion.

Authorization verification:
1. Retrieve the comment by commentId from discussion_board_comments table
2. Verify the comment exists and is not already deleted (deleted_at is null)
3. Check if the authenticated user is the comment author by comparing discussion_board_member_id
4. If not the author, verify the user has administrator privileges
5. Reject with 403 Forbidden if authorization fails

Deletion process:
1. Update the comment record by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
2. This implements soft deletion to preserve audit trail
3. The comment will no longer appear in active comment lists
4. Related data (article reference) remains intact

Error handling:
- Return 404 Not Found if comment does not exist
- Return 404 Not Found if comment is already deleted
- Return 403 Forbidden if user is not authorized (not author and not admin)
- Return 401 Unauthorized if user is not authenticated

The articleId parameter is used to establish the hierarchical path structure but the actual deletion operates on the comment record directly.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a specific comment from an article in the discussion board.

This operation removes a comment from the discussion_board_comments table, completely deleting the comment content and removing it from all article views. The comment will no longer be accessible through any API operations or user interfaces.

Authorization is enforced based on comment ownership and user roles. Only the original author of the comment or an administrator can delete the comment. When a member deletes their own comment, the system permanently removes it from all articles. When an administrator deletes a comment, the system removes it regardless of the original author.

The comment must exist and not already be deleted. If the comment does not exist or has already been deleted, the system rejects the request with an appropriate error. Banned users cannot delete content, and the system enforces this restriction by checking account status before allowing the operation.

This operation is part of the comment management workflow, complementing comment creation, viewing, and editing operations. It ensures users maintain control over their own content while administrators retain moderation capabilities.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of comment snapshots for a specific comment within an article.

This operation provides access to the historical revision trail of a comment, capturing all point-in-time snapshots that were automatically created when the comment was modified. Each snapshot preserves the exact state of the comment at the moment it was captured, including the content, timestamps, and author information.

Snapshots are system-generated and read-only. They serve as an audit trail for content moderation, enabling administrators to review comment changes over time and recover previous versions if needed. The snapshots denormalize all parent comment fields to preserve historical accuracy even if the original comment or its relationships change later.

Access requires authentication as a member or administrator. Guests can view snapshots when browsing articles. The operation supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by snapshot timestamp or other fields.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId} for retrieving the current comment state, and PATCH /articles/{articleId}/comments for listing all comments on an article.

This enables content moderation audits, historical content recovery, and version control for comment discussions.

The snapshot contains denormalized references to the article and member who authored the comment, captured at the time the snapshot was taken. This ensures the historical record remains accurate even if the parent comment's relationships change later. The snapshot includes the comment content, original creation timestamp, last update timestamp, and the exact time when this snapshot was captured.

Access to comment snapshots requires valid article and comment context. The article ID, comment ID, and snapshot ID parameters ensure proper hierarchical navigation and data isolation. This operation is useful for administrators reviewing content changes, recovering previous versions of comments, or auditing comment modification history.

Related operations include retrieving all snapshots for a comment, viewing the current comment state, and listing all comments on an article.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrator privilege escalation requests.

This operation enables users to search and browse administrator promotion requests with flexible filtering options. Members can view only their own submitted requests, while administrators have access to view all requests across the platform. The search supports filtering by request status (pending, approved, rejected), submission date ranges, and other criteria.

The response includes summarized request information optimized for list displays, including request ID, submitting member details, status, submission timestamp, and review information when available. For approved or rejected requests, the reviewing administrator information is included.

Security considerations ensure proper data isolation: regular members can only access their own requests, while administrators can view the complete request history. Super administrators have full access to all requests regardless of status.

This operation is commonly used together with GET /admin-requests/{requestId} to retrieve detailed information about a specific request after identifying it in the list view.

For authorization:

- If actor is administrator: No member ID filter applied, return all requests

Join with discussion_board_members to include member information (email, display name) in the response.
Join with discussion_board_administrators (left join) to include reviewing administrator information when reviewed_at is not null.

Apply sorting based on request parameters (default: submitted_at descending).
Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based pagination as configured.

Return paginated response with IPageIDiscussionBoardAdminRequest.ISummary structure containing pagination metadata and data array.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator privilege escalation request by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete information about an administrator request, including the applicant's reason for requesting elevated privileges, the current status of the request (pending, approved, or rejected), submission timestamp, and review details if a decision has been made. The response includes the applicant's information and, if applicable, the decision context provided by the reviewing super administrator.

Access to this endpoint is restricted based on user role and request ownership. Regular members can only view their own administrator requests to check the status of their applications. Administrators and super administrators can view any administrator request as part of their governance and review responsibilities. This enables members to track their application progress and allows administrators to review request details before making approval or rejection decisions.

The request status indicates the current state: 'pending' means the request is awaiting super administrator review, 'approved' indicates the member has been promoted to regular administrator status, and 'rejected' means the request was denied and the member retains their current permissions. When a decision has been made, the response includes the decision type and any additional context provided by the reviewing super administrator.

Related operations include PATCH /admin-requests for listing and filtering requests, POST /admin-requests for submitting new requests, and GET /admin-requests/{requestId}/decision for detailed decision information.

1. Verify the requesting user is authenticated and is a member (not guest, not administrator)
2. Check that the user is not banned by querying discussion_board_ban_records for active bans
3. Query discussion_board_admin_requests to ensure no existing pending request exists for this member (status = 'pending')
4. Validate that the reason field is not empty and contains meaningful text

**Database Operations**:

1. Insert new record into discussion_board_admin_requests with:
   - id: Generate new UUID
   - discussion_board_member_id: Set to authenticated user's ID from session
   - discussion_board_administrator_id: NULL (not yet reviewed)

   - created_at: Current timestamp
   - updated_at: Current timestamp
   - deleted_at: NULL

2. Return the created request entity with all fields

**Error Handling**:

- Return 401 Unauthorized if user is not authenticated
- Return 403 Forbidden if user is a guest, already an administrator, or banned
- Return 409 Conflict if user already has a pending request
- Return 400 Bad Request if reason is empty or missing
- Return 500 Internal Server Error for database operation failures

**Transaction Considerations**:

The insert operation should be wrapped in a database transaction to ensure data consistency. If validation fails at any point, no database changes should occur.
operations.description:
Submit an administrator privilege escalation request from a registered member.

This operation allows registered members to apply for administrator privileges by submitting a written justification for why they should be elevated to an administrator role. The request enters a pending state and awaits review by a super administrator.

**Authorization and Access Control**:

Only authenticated members with regular user privileges can submit administrator requests. The system enforces several restrictions: guests cannot submit requests, users who already possess administrator privileges cannot submit requests, and banned users are prohibited from submitting requests. Additionally, members with existing pending requests cannot submit duplicate requests.

**Request Validation**:

The request requires a non-empty reason field where the member explains their qualifications and motivations for seeking administrator privileges. The reason text is preserved exactly as submitted and becomes part of the permanent request record visible to super administrators during the review process.

**Related Operations**:

After submission, the requesting member can track their request status using GET /admin-requests/{requestId}. Super administrators can view all pending requests using PATCH /admin-requests with appropriate filters, and can approve or reject requests using dedicated decision endpoints. The approval process is documented in the Super Administrator Review Process requirements.

**Request Lifecycle**:

Upon successful submission, the request is created with 'pending' status and a submission timestamp. The request remains in pending state until a super administrator reviews and makes a decision (approve or reject). The complete request history is preserved for audit purposes.

The response includes detailed information about each decision: the decision type (approved or rejected), the reviewing super administrator's identity, the requesting member's information, the original request reason, and the timestamp when the decision was made. This enables governance oversight by allowing super administrators to review enforcement patterns across different reviewers and maintain accountability for all privilege escalation decisions.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to super administrators only, as it contains sensitive audit information about the organization's governance processes. Regular administrators and members cannot view these decision records. The operation supports filtering by decision type, date ranges, and specific reviewers to enable targeted oversight and reporting.

Related operations include viewing individual admin requests and managing administrator accounts. This decisions endpoint complements those operations by providing a centralized view of all decision-making activities in the privilege escalation workflow.

Each decision is linked to exactly one administrator request and one super administrator who made the decision. Once a decision is recorded, it cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring accountability and traceability of all administrator promotion activities.

This endpoint is typically used by super administrators to review past decisions, by system administrators to audit the privilege escalation process, or by the system to display decision details in administrative interfaces. Create a new admin request decision record in discussion_board_admin_request_decisions table.

**Authorization**:
- Verify the authenticated user is a super administrator (grade = 'super')
- Reject if user is not authenticated or not a super administrator

**Validation**:
1. Verify the admin request exists and is not soft-deleted
2. Verify the request status is 'pending' - reject if already approved or rejected
3. Validate decision_type is either 'approved' or 'rejected'
4. Ensure no existing decision record exists for this request (unique constraint)

**Transaction**:
1. Create new decision record with:
   - discussion_board_admin_request_id from path parameter
   - discussion_board_administrator_id from authenticated super admin
   - decision_type from request body
   - decision_context from request body (nullable)
   - created_at and updated_at timestamps
2. Update the parent admin request:
   - Set status to 'approved' or 'rejected' based on decision_type
   - Set reviewed_at to current timestamp
   - Set discussion_board_administrator_id to the reviewer's ID
3. If decision_type is 'approved', promote the member to regular administrator:
   - Create new record in discussion_board_administrators with grade='regular'
   - Copy email, display_name, bio from the member record

**Error Handling**:
- Return 404 if admin request not found or soft-deleted
- Return 409 if request already has a decision (not pending)
- Return 403 if user is not a super administrator
- Return 400 if decision_type is invalid
- Return 409 if user attempting to decide on their own request
operations.description:
Create an approval or rejection decision for an administrator privilege escalation request.

This operation allows super administrators to review and decide on pending administrator promotion requests submitted by regular members. When a super administrator creates a decision, the system records the decision type (approved or rejected), optional context notes, and automatically updates the request status.

**Authorization Requirements**:
Only super administrators can create decisions on admin requests. Regular administrators and members are prohibited from accessing this endpoint. The system verifies the authenticated user's administrator grade before processing the request.

**Decision Workflow**:
When a decision is created, the system performs several actions atomically within a database transaction. The decision record is created in the discussion_board_admin_request_decisions table, linking the requesting member, the reviewing super administrator, and the decision outcome. The parent admin request status is automatically updated from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected', and the review timestamp is recorded.

**Approval Consequences**:
If the decision type is 'approved', the system automatically promotes the requesting member to a regular administrator. A new administrator account is created with the member's email, display name, and bio, with the grade set to 'regular'. The member immediately gains administrator privileges including section management and content moderation capabilities.

**Rejection Consequences**:
If the decision type is 'rejected', the member retains their existing permissions without any elevation. The rejected request record is preserved for potential future review, and the member may submit a new administrator request at a later time.

**Idempotency and Constraints**:
Each admin request can have at most one decision due to the unique constraint on discussion_board_admin_request_id in the decisions table. Once a decision is recorded, the request status changes and no further decisions are allowed. This prevents duplicate processing and ensures audit trail integrity.

**Related Operations**:
- `PATCH /admin-requests` - List admin requests with filtering by status
- `GET /admin-requests/{requestId}` - View specific admin request details
- `POST /admin-requests` - Submit a new admin request (member action)

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of ban records from the discussion board platform.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for reviewing user suspension history. Ban records are audit trail entries that document when users (members or administrators) were banned, the reason for the ban, which administrator imposed it, and when the ban was lifted.

The operation supports filtering by ban status (active or lifted), actor type (member or administrator), date ranges for ban timestamps, and text search on ban reasons. Results are returned with cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large datasets.

Only authenticated administrators have access to this endpoint. The returned ban record summaries include essential information such as the banned user identifier, ban reason, timestamps, and the administrator who imposed the ban. For detailed information about a specific ban record, use the GET /banRecords/{banRecordId} endpoint.

This operation is part of the moderation and audit functionality, enabling administrators to review enforcement actions, track ban history for specific users, and maintain accountability for moderation decisions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_ban_records table with pagination and filtering support.

1. Parse request body for search criteria: actor_type filter, ban status filter (active vs lifted based on unbanned_at null check), banned_at date range, ban_reason text search.

2. Apply authorization check: verify the requesting user is an authenticated administrator (regular or super).

3. Build query with filters:
   - actor_type: exact match on 'member' or 'administrator'
   - status: filter by unbanned_at IS NULL (active) or IS NOT NULL (lifted)
   - banned_at range: BETWEEN start and end timestamps
   - ban_reason: ILIKE search with %text% for partial matching

4. Apply sorting: default by banned_at DESC (most recent first), support custom sort fields.

5. Apply pagination: use cursor-based pagination with limit (default 20, max 100) and cursor parameters.

6. Join with discussion_board_administrators to fetch banned_by display_name for the summary.

7. For actor_type='member', optionally join with discussion_board_ban_record_of_members to get member details.

8. For actor_type='administrator', optionally join with discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators to get administrator details.

9. Return paginated results with metadata: current page, total count, has_next, next_cursor.

10. Handle edge cases: empty results, invalid filter combinations, missing cursor values.

11. Log access for audit trail: record which administrator viewed which ban records.

When a ban is created, the system records the ban reason, timestamp, and which administrator imposed the ban. The banned user will be prevented from logging in to the platform.

The ban record maintains a complete audit trail for moderation accountability. All existing articles and comments written by the banned user are preserved in the system, ensuring content history is maintained even when user accounts are suspended.

Administrators must provide a detailed ban reason explaining the policy violation or harmful behavior that warranted the ban. This reason is stored for potential appeal purposes and audit trail maintenance. The system prevents duplicate ban records for users who are already banned.

This operation requires administrator authentication and appropriate privileges. Only authenticated administrators can create ban records. The operation links the ban to either a member account or administrator account through the polymorphic ownership pattern.

The ban record maintains critical audit information including the ban reason, the timestamp when the ban was imposed (banned_at), and the administrator who imposed the ban (banned_by). These fields are immutable to ensure the integrity of the moderation audit trail.

Security considerations: Only administrators with appropriate privileges can update ban records. The system validates that the requesting administrator has sufficient clearance to modify ban records. Regular members and guests cannot access this operation.

4. If updating ban_reason: Allow only if the ban is still active (unbanned_at is null). Update the ban_reason field with the new value.
5. Update the updated_at timestamp automatically.
6. Return the updated ban record with full details including related administrator and user information.
7. Handle edge cases: Ban record not found (404), insufficient privileges (403), attempting to modify immutable fields (400), ban already lifted (400 if trying to unban again).

The banned_at, banned_by, and actor_type fields are immutable and cannot be modified through this operation to preserve audit trail integrity.

Assign one or more tags to an existing article for categorization and search purposes.

This operation allows article authors to add free-text tags to their own articles. Tags serve as organizational labels that enable article filtering, discovery, and topic-based navigation across the discussion board platform. Each tag assignment creates a persistent link between the article and the tag, stored in the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

Authorization requires that the requesting user must be the author of the target article. The system validates ownership by comparing the authenticated session's member ID against the article's discussion_board_member_id field. This restriction ensures that only content creators can manage their own article's categorization.

Tag names are free-text entries with no predefined vocabulary or approval process. The system automatically creates new tag records when a user assigns a tag name that doesn't yet exist in the discussion_board_tags table. Duplicate tag assignments to the same article are prevented by the composite unique constraint on article_id and tag_id.

Related operations include viewing article tags via GET /articles/{articleId}/tags, updating tags via PUT /articles/{articleId}/tags, and removing tags via DELETE /articles/{articleId}/tags/{tagId}.

operations.description:
Remove a specific tag assignment from an article.

This operation deletes the association between a tag and an article by removing the corresponding record from the discussion_board_article_tags junction table. The tag itself is not deleted from the system and remains available for assignment to other articles.

Security and authorization:

- Only the article's author (the member who created the article) can remove tags from their own articles
- Administrators can remove tags from any article regardless of authorship
- The system verifies ownership before allowing the operation
- Banned users cannot perform any article modification operations

Database impact:

- The operation removes one record from discussion_board_article_tags
- The article (discussion_board_articles) remains unchanged
- The tag (discussion_board_tags) remains unchanged and available for other articles
- If this was the last assignment of the tag, the tag still persists in the system

Related operations:

- GET /articles/{articleId}/tags retrieves all tags currently assigned to an article
- PATCH /articles/{articleId}/tags assigns multiple tags to an article
- GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves the full article including its tags
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate path parameters: articleId and tagId must be valid UUIDs

2. Verify authentication: Request must include valid member or administrator session token

3. Fetch the article by articleId from discussion_board_articles table
   - Check if article exists
   - Check if article is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)

4. Verify authorization:
   - If requester is a member: verify they are the article's author (discussion_board_member_id matches)
   - If requester is an administrator: allow operation regardless of authorship
   - If requester is banned: reject the operation

5. Fetch the tag assignment record from discussion_board_article_tags:
   - Query where discussion_board_article_id = articleId AND discussion_board_tag_id = tagId
   - If no record exists, return 404 Not Found

6. Delete the tag assignment record from discussion_board_article_tags

7. Return 204 No Content with empty body

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or missing authentication
- 403 Forbidden: User is not authorized to modify this article's tags
- 404 Not Found: Article not found, tag not found, or tag assignment does not exist
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid UUID format in path parameters

operations.name: patchByTagid
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_articles table joined with discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags tables.

1. Validate tagId exists in discussion_board_tags and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
2. Join discussion_board_articles with discussion_board_article_tags on article id
3. Filter by discussion_board_tag_id matching the provided tagId
4. Apply soft-delete filter on articles (deleted_at is null) unless explicitly requested
5. Apply search filters from request body:
   - Title/content text search using trigram indexes
   - Date range filtering on created_at
   - Section filtering if specified
6. Apply pagination: limit and offset based on page and pageSize
7. Apply sorting: default by created_at descending, support custom sort fields
8. Return article summaries with tag information included

Authorization: Any authenticated user (member or administrator) can access. Guests cannot access this endpoint.

Edge cases:
- Return empty result set if tag has no articles
- Return 404 if tagId does not exist or is soft-deleted
- Handle pagination gracefully for large result sets
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of articles associated with a specific tag.

This operation enables users to discover and browse articles that have been categorized with a particular tag. Tags serve as free-text labels for informal content organization, allowing users to group articles by topics, themes, or custom categories. The tag system supports case-sensitive identifiers and allows multiple tags per article.

The operation supports advanced search capabilities including title and content text matching, date range filtering, and customizable sorting options. Results are returned in a paginated format with configurable page sizes to handle large result sets efficiently.

Security: This operation requires user authentication. Only registered members and administrators can access articles by tag. Guest users cannot perform this operation.

Related operations:
- `GET /tags/{tagId}` retrieves detailed tag information
- `PATCH /articles` lists all articles with broader search criteria
- `GET /articles/{articleId}` retrieves a specific article with all its tags

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of administrator privilege escalation requests that are currently awaiting super administrator review.

This operation provides super administrators with visibility into all pending admin promotion requests submitted by members seeking elevated permissions. Each request includes the submitting member's display name, their justification for becoming an administrator, and the submission timestamp.

The endpoint filters requests to show only those with 'pending' status, excluding already approved or rejected requests. Super administrators use this list to review and make decisions on privilege escalation requests, either approving to promote the member to regular administrator or rejecting to maintain their current user status.

Access is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators and members cannot view pending admin requests. The response includes pagination metadata to support browsing through large numbers of pending requests efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_admin_requests table for records where status equals 'pending'.

Join with discussion_board_members table using discussion_board_member_id to retrieve the submitting member's display_name for each request.

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach based on IRequest parameters (page, pageSize, sortBy, sortOrder).

Sort results by submitted_at in descending order by default to show most recent requests first.

Return summary objects containing: id, member's display_name, reason, status, submitted_at, and reviewed_at (null for pending).

Include pagination metadata: currentPage, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages.

Validate that the authenticated user has super administrator role before executing the query.

Handle empty result set by returning empty data array with pagination metadata showing zero total items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending administrator request summaries

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for the pending requests list

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of articles filtered by tag criteria.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for finding articles based on tag assignments. Users can filter articles by specific tags, enabling topic-based content discovery across the discussion board platform.

The search supports multiple tag filtering strategies including exact tag matches and tag name patterns. Results are returned with pagination support for efficient browsing of large result sets. Each article summary includes associated tag information for display purposes.

This operation is accessible to all authenticated users (guest, member, and administrator) as tag-based article filtering is a core content discovery feature. The underlying discussion_board_articles table contains article content with soft deletion support, while discussion_board_tags stores unique tag names and discussion_board_article_tags manages the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} for viewing full article details, PATCH /articles for general article search with additional filters, and PATCH /tags for browsing available tags in the system.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering articles by tags with pagination parameters

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summaries with tag information

operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_articles table with tag-based filtering through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table.

Implementation steps:
1. Parse the request body to extract tag filter criteria (tag IDs or tag names) and pagination parameters
2. Join discussion_board_articles with discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags to enable tag filtering
3. Apply soft deletion filter (deleted_at IS NULL) to exclude deleted articles
4. Apply tag filters based on request criteria:
   - If specific tag IDs provided: filter by tag IDs using IN clause
   - If tag name patterns provided: filter by tag names using ILIKE or pattern matching
   - Support for multiple tag filters (AND/OR logic based on request)
5. Apply additional filters if specified (section, author, date range, text search)
6. Apply sorting based on request parameters (default: created_at DESC)
7. Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset-based approach
8. Return paginated results with article summaries including associated tag names
9. Include pagination metadata (total count, page info, cursor for next page)

Edge cases:
- Handle empty tag filter (return all articles if no tags specified)
- Handle non-existent tag IDs gracefully (return empty result set)
- Ensure soft-deleted articles are never returned
- Support case-insensitive tag name matching
- Optimize queries with proper indexes on tag_id and article_id columns

IDiscussionBoardAdministrator.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for querying and filtering administrator accounts.

This type defines the query parameters for the administrator listing operation. It supports pagination, filtering by administrator grade, searching by email or display name, and custom sorting. All parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction.

**Pagination**:

Use `page` and `limit` to control result set size. Page numbers are 1-indexed. The limit parameter accepts values from 1 to 100, with a default typically set by the server.

**Filtering**:

The `grade` parameter filters administrators by their privilege level. Valid values are 'regular' for standard administrators and 'super' for super administrators with elevated permissions.

**Search**:

The `search` parameter performs a text search across email addresses and display names. This is useful for finding specific administrators quickly.

**Sorting**:

Use `sortBy` and `sortOrder` to control result ordering. The sortBy parameter accepts column names like 'created_at', 'email', 'display_name', or 'grade'. The sortOrder parameter accepts 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering articles in the discussion board platform.

This type defines the query parameters for article listing operations, enabling users to search, filter, paginate, and sort article results. All properties are optional, allowing flexible combinations of search criteria.

**Search and Filtering**:

- **Text Search**: Search across article titles and content using full-text matching with trigram similarity for partial matches
- **Section Filter**: Filter articles by a specific section ID to browse content within a topic category
- **Tag Filter**: Filter by one or more tag IDs (articles must have ALL specified tags - AND logic)
- **Author Filter**: Filter articles by a specific member ID to view content from a particular user
- **Date Range Filter**: Filter articles by creation date range to find content within specific time periods

**Pagination**:

- **Page**: Request a specific page number (1-indexed) for paginated results
- **Limit**: Specify the number of articles per page (1-100, default 20)

**Sorting**:

- **Sort By**: Choose which field to sort by (creation date, update date, or title)
- **Sort Order**: Specify ascending or descending order (default is descending for newest first)

**Usage Examples**:

- Search for articles containing "climate": `{ search: "climate" }`
- Filter by section with pagination: `{ section_id: "uuid", page: 2, limit: 50 }`
- Find recent articles by author: `{ author_id: "uuid", sortBy: "createdAt", sortOrder: "desc" }`
- Multi-filter query: `{ section_id: "uuid", tag_ids: ["uuid1", "uuid2"], from_date: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }`
IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameters for article listing and search operations on discussion_board_articles table.

**Search Implementation**:
- search: Apply trigram similarity matching on title and content columns (minimum 2 chars, maximum 100 chars)
- section_id: JOIN discussion_board_sections, filter where discussion_board_section_id matches and section is active (deleted_at IS NULL)
- tag_ids: JOIN discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags, filter by tag IDs with AND logic (article must have ALL specified tags)
- author_id: JOIN discussion_board_members, filter where discussion_board_member_id matches
- from_date/to_date: Filter created_at BETWEEN from_date AND to_date (inclusive)

**Pagination**:
- page: 1-indexed page number, minimum 1, default 1
- limit: Items per page, minimum 1, maximum 100, default 20
- Calculate offset as (page - 1) * limit

**Sorting**:
- sortBy: Field name for ORDER BY clause, valid values: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'title'
- sortOrder: 'asc' or 'desc', default 'desc'
- Default sort: ORDER BY created_at DESC

**Business Rules**:
- Always filter deleted_at IS NULL for non-admin users
- Admin users can optionally include soft-deleted articles (handled separately, not in this DTO)
- Validate section_id, tag_ids, author_id reference existing records
- Return empty array for no results (not an error)

IDiscussionBoardArticleSnapshot.description:
A point-in-time snapshot of an article capturing its complete state at the moment of modification for audit trail and revision history purposes.

Article snapshots are immutable historical records that preserve the exact title, content, author, and section assignment when an article was modified. They enable organizations to maintain compliance audit trails, track content modifications over time, and understand the evolution of article content through revision history.

Each snapshot contains the article's title, full content text, author information, section assignment, and the exact timestamp when the snapshot was created. Snapshots are append-only and never modified or deleted after creation, ensuring the integrity of the audit trail.

Access to snapshots is controlled by the underlying article's visibility and user permissions - guests can view snapshots of public articles, members can view snapshots of their own articles and public articles, and administrators can view all article snapshots.

Relations exposed as objects: article (via discussion_board_article_id FK), author (via discussion_board_member_id FK), section (via discussion_board_section_id FK). Excluded: discussion_board_member_session_id (server-managed session context for audit trail), session relation (derived from session FK). All fields required as snapshots are immutable historical records created during article modifications.

IDiscussionBoardArticleSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and paginating article snapshots.

This type defines the search criteria and pagination controls for retrieving article revision history. Article snapshots are point-in-time records captured when articles are modified, providing an audit trail of content changes.

Available filters:
- **search**: Text search matching against snapshot titles
- **authorId**: Filter snapshots by specific author (member ID)
- **from/to**: Date range filter for snapshot creation timestamps
- **page/limit**: Pagination controls for large result sets
- **sort**: Ordering preference (default: newest first)

All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, returns all snapshots for the article sorted by creation date descending. The article itself is identified by the path parameter, not included in this request body.

- authorId: equality filter on discussion_board_member_id column
- from: lower bound filter on created_at (created_at >= from)
- to: upper bound filter on created_at (created_at <= to)
- page: pagination page number (1-indexed, default: 1)
- limit: results per page (default: 20, max: 100)
- sort: sort field and direction (default: 'created_at desc')

Article ID comes from path parameter {articleId}, not request body.

Validation rules:
- page >= 1
- limit >= 1 and <= 100

- sort must be valid field name (created_at, title)

All fields are optional. When no filters provided, returns all snapshots for the article sorted by created_at descending.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Complete comment entity with full details including content, timestamps, and author information.

This type represents a user-generated comment attached to a discussion board article. Comments enable community discussions and are displayed in chronological order. Each comment is authored by a registered member and permanently associated with a specific article.

The comment includes the full text content, creation and modification timestamps, and references to both the author (member who wrote it) and the article (parent resource). Soft deletion is supported via the deleted_at field - when present, the comment is logically deleted but preserved for audit purposes.

Authorization is enforced at the comment level: only the comment's author or administrators can view full details. This protects user privacy while enabling content moderation.

A point-in-time snapshot of a comment's state from the revision history.

Comment snapshots capture the exact state of a comment at a specific moment in time, including all field values and foreign key references. This enables content moderation audits, historical content recovery, and version control for comment discussions. The snapshot preserves the comment content, original creation timestamp, last update timestamp, and the exact time when the snapshot was captured.

The snapshot contains denormalized references to the article and the member who authored the comment, captured at the time the snapshot was taken. This ensures the historical record remains accurate even if the parent comment's relationships change later. The commentId field references the parent comment that this snapshot belongs to.

Snapshots are automatically created when comments are created or modified, providing a complete audit trail of all comment changes over time.

IDiscussionBoardTag.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating the list of tags used across the discussion board platform.

This request object provides flexible search and filtering capabilities for discovering tags. Tags are free-text labels that users assign to articles for categorization and content discovery. The request supports multiple filtering dimensions:

**Search**: Partial text matching on tag names, allowing users to find tags by entering keywords or partial text.

**Date Range**: Filter tags by their creation date using createdAfter and createdBefore parameters, useful for discovering recently added tags or tags from specific time periods.

**Deletion Status**: By default, only active tags are returned. Set includeDeleted to true to also show soft-deleted tags.

**Usage Filter**: Set excludeUnused to true to filter out tags that have no associated articles, showing only tags currently in use.

**Pagination**: Control the number of results and navigate through pages using page and limit parameters. Default page size is 20 with a maximum of 100 items per page.

**Sorting**: Sort results by tag name (alphabetically) or creation date (newest or oldest first).

All parameters are optional, allowing users to retrieve all tags without any filtering by sending an empty request body.
IDiscussionBoardTag.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Request DTO for filtering and paginating tag listings. This schema defines query parameters for the PATCH /discussionBoard/tags endpoint.

Query Parameter Mapping:
- search: Partial text matching on discussion_board_tags.name using LIKE query
- page: Page number for offset-based pagination (1-indexed, default 1)
- limit: Items per page (min 1, max 100, default 20)
- sortBy: Sort field, options: 'name' or 'created_at' (default 'created_at')
- sortOrder: Sort direction, options: 'asc' or 'desc' (default 'desc')
- createdAfter: Filter tags created after this datetime (discussion_board_tags.created_at >= value)
- createdBefore: Filter tags created before this datetime (discussion_board_tags.created_at <= value)
- includeDeleted: When true, include soft-deleted tags (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Default false shows only active tags.
- excludeUnused: When true, exclude tags with no associated articles via LEFT JOIN discussion_board_article_tags

Query Construction:
SELECT * FROM discussion_board_tags
WHERE (deleted_at IS NULL OR includeDeleted = true)
  AND (search IS NULL OR name LIKE %search%)
  AND (createdAfter IS NULL OR created_at >= createdAfter)
  AND (createdBefore IS NULL OR created_at <= createdBefore)
  AND (excludeUnused IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM discussion_board_article_tags WHERE tag_id = id))
ORDER BY sortBy sortOrder
LIMIT limit OFFSET (page - 1) * limit

All parameters are optional. Empty request returns all active tags with default pagination.

- Listing articles by specific tag

IDiscussionBoardSection.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and browsing discussion board sections.

This type defines the query parameters for the section listing operation, which allows users to search, filter, sort, and paginate through the organizational sections that categorize articles by topic.

**Search and Filtering**:
- Use the `search` parameter to find sections by name or description using partial text matching
- Only active sections (not soft-deleted) are returned

**Pagination**:
- `page`: Specifies which page of results to retrieve (default: 1)
- `limit`: Number of sections per page (default: 20, maximum: 100)

**Sorting**:
- `sort`: Field to sort by - options are `id`, `name`, `created_at`, or `updated_at` (default: `created_at`)
- `direction`: Sort order - `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending (default: `desc`)

**Access**: This operation is available to all users including guests (no authentication required).
IDiscussionBoardSection.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameter DTO for section listing operation.

**Search Logic**:
- search: Applies LIKE pattern matching on both name and description fields
- If search is empty or null, no filtering is applied

**Pagination Logic**:
- page: Page number (1-indexed), default is 1
- limit: Items per page, default is 20, maximum is 100
- Calculate offset: (page - 1) * limit

**Sorting Logic**:
- sort: Field name to sort by (id, name, created_at, updated_at), default is created_at
- direction: Sort direction (asc, desc), default is desc
- Validate that sort field is in allowed list

**Soft Delete Filter**:
- Always apply WHERE deleted_at IS NULL to exclude deleted sections

**Validation**:
- page must be >= 1
- limit must be >= 1 and <= 100
- sort must be one of: id, name, created_at, updated_at
- direction must be one of: asc, desc

Complete article entity from the discussion board platform.

This type represents a full article with all its content and associated metadata. Each article belongs to exactly one section for organizational categorization and is authored by a registered member. The article includes the title, full text content, creation and update timestamps, and soft-delete status.

The response includes the article's section details (name, description), author information (display name, bio), all associated tags for categorization and filtering, and the total count of comments. Articles support soft deletion to preserve historical data while removing from active listings.

All users including guests can view articles, supporting the platform's open browsing model. Articles are the primary content units that users create, organize by sections, and engage with through comments.

This type represents a time-limited, single-use token generated when a user requests to reset their password. The token is sent to the user's registered email address and can be used to verify identity and allow password change without requiring current credentials.

The response includes the token's current status (unused, used, or expired), creation timestamp, expiration time, and the associated user account information. Audit information such as user agent and IP address from the original reset request is also included for security monitoring purposes.

Access to password reset records requires appropriate authentication. Administrators can view any password reset record for security auditing, while regular members can only access their own password reset tokens. Token values should be masked or partially hidden in responses to prevent unauthorized access to the actual token strings.
IDiscussionBoardAdministratorPasswordRes.x-autobe-specification:
This is a polymorphic response type that combines data from two separate tables: discussion_board_member_password_resets and discussion_board_administrator_password_resets.

Implementation:
1. Query both tables by the resetId parameter
2. If found in member table: set owner to member.ISummary, user_agent and ip_address from member table, token_type and updated_at as null
3. If found in administrator table: set owner to administrator.ISummary, token_type and updated_at from admin table, user_agent and ip_address as null
4. Map expires_at (admin) to expired_at in response for consistency
5. Token should be masked or partially hidden in actual response for security
6. Include computed 'status' field based on used_at and expired_at values: 'unused' (used_at is null and not expired), 'used' (used_at is set), 'expired' (expired_at < current time)
7. Join with member or administrator table to populate owner object with email, displayName, id

IDiscussionBoardAdministratorPasswordRes.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering password reset records across the discussion board platform.

This request body allows administrators to query password reset activity with flexible filtering options. You can filter by user type (members or administrators), token status (used or unused), and date ranges. Search capabilities include filtering by email address, user ID, IP address, or user agent string.

Pagination parameters control the result set size and ordering. All fields are optional, allowing you to retrieve all records or apply any combination of filters. This is particularly useful for security audits, investigating suspicious password reset activity, or responding to account security incidents.

Access to this operation requires administrator authentication and all queries are logged for audit compliance.

Filter logic:
- user_type: 'member' queries discussion_board_member_password_resets, 'administrator' queries discussion_board_administrator_password_resets, omit to query both tables
- status: 'used' filters where used_at IS NOT NULL, 'unused' filters where used_at IS NULL
- created_at_from/to: filter by created_at column range (inclusive)
- search_email: LIKE query on email from joined member or administrator tables
- search_user_id: filter by discussion_board_members_id or discussion_board_administrators_id (UUID)
- search_ip_address: LIKE on ip_address column (member password resets only)
- search_user_agent: LIKE on user_agent column (member password resets only)

Pagination:
- page: default 1, minimum 1, 1-indexed
- limit: default 20, minimum 1, maximum 100
- sort: field name for ordering (created_at, expired_at, used_at, user_email, etc.)
- direction: 'asc' or 'desc', default 'desc'

Security: All access to this endpoint is logged for audit trail compliance.

IDiscussionBoardAdministratorSession.ISu.description:
Lightweight session summary for displaying authentication sessions in administrative views.

This type represents a unified view of sessions across all actor types (guest, member, administrator) in the discussion board system. It includes essential session metadata such as session identifier, actor type discriminator, connection information (IP address, URL, referrer), and temporal data (creation and expiration timestamps).

The actor_type field distinguishes between the three session types, and the actor field provides a reference to the authenticated user's summary information. This summary is designed for listing and filtering purposes in administrative dashboards, security auditing, and session management operations.

Sensitive authentication data (token hashes, token expiration times) are excluded from this summary as they are not needed for display purposes and should not be exposed in listing operations.
IDiscussionBoardAdministratorSession.ISu.x-autobe-specification:
Unified session summary aggregating data from three session tables via UNION ALL: discussion_board_guest_sessions, discussion_board_member_sessions, discussion_board_administrator_sessions.

- id: Direct from session table id column (UUID). Source: discussion_board_guest_sessions.id, discussion_board_member_sessions.id, or discussion_board_administrator_sessions.id depending on session type.
- actor_type: Computed discriminator based on source table ('guest', 'member', 'administrator')
- ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at: Direct from session table columns
- actor: JOIN to corresponding actor table (discussion_board_guests, discussion_board_members, or discussion_board_administrators) and return ISummary

- access_token_hash, refresh_token_hash: Security-sensitive token hashes
- access_token_expires_at, refresh_token_expires_at: Token expiration times (not needed in summary)

Excluded FK columns (exposed via actor object):
- discussion_board_guest_id, discussion_board_member_id, discussion_board_administrator_id

Query logic: UNION ALL across three session tables with actor_type discriminator, JOIN to appropriate actor table based on session type.

IDiscussionBoardAdministratorPasswordRes.description:
Lightweight summary of a password reset request for security audit listings.

This type represents a unified view of password reset records from both member and administrator accounts, enabling administrators to monitor password reset activity across the entire discussion board platform. Each record includes essential information for security auditing: user identification (type, ID, email), the reset token, lifecycle timestamps (created, expired, used), and security context (IP address, user agent).

The is_used field indicates whether the token has been redeemed for a password change. Records with null used_at values represent pending or expired reset requests that haven't been used, while non-null values indicate successful password resets.

This summary type is optimized for list views and filtering operations, excluding sensitive data and large text fields. For detailed password reset information, use the full IDiscussionBoardPasswordReset type.

IDiscussionBoardAdministratorSession.description:
Detailed session information including connection metadata, temporal boundaries, and associated user information.

This type represents a unified view of user sessions across all actor types (guest, member, administrator). It includes the session identifier, the associated user's ID and type, connection metadata (IP address, entry URL, referrer), and temporal information (creation and expiration timestamps).

The is_active field indicates whether the session is currently valid (not expired). For administrator sessions, additional token expiration metadata is available including access token and refresh token expiration times.

Aggregate session data from three session tables based on sessionId parameter:

1. Query discussion_board_guest_sessions, discussion_board_member_sessions, and discussion_board_administrator_sessions to find matching session by id
2. Determine user_type based on which table returned the session (guest, member, or administrator)
3. Join with corresponding user table (discussion_board_guests, discussion_board_members, discussion_board_administrators) to get user_id
4. Compute is_active: true if expired_at is null or expired_at > current_time, false otherwise
5. For administrator sessions only, include access_token_expires_at and refresh_token_expires_at from discussion_board_administrator_sessions

- If session not found in any table, return 404
- If expired_at is null, session is still active
- Token expiration fields should be null for non-administrator sessions
- IP, href, and referrer may be null if not captured during session creation

This type supports comprehensive session querying for administrative purposes including security auditing and user activity monitoring. It enables filtering by session status (active or expired), actor type (member, administrator, or guest), specific actor identification, date ranges for session creation and expiration times, and IP address for security investigations.

All parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction. Pagination is supported with configurable page size (default 20, maximum 100). Results can be sorted by creation time or expiration time in ascending or descending order.
IDiscussionBoardAdministratorSession.IRe.x-autobe-specification:
Request DTO for filtering and paginating session listings across all actor types (guest, member, administrator). This schema does not map to a single database table but provides query parameters for aggregating data from discussion_board_guest_sessions, discussion_board_member_sessions, and discussion_board_administrator_sessions tables.

Query logic:
- status: Filter sessions by expiration state (active if expired_at is null, expired otherwise)
- actor_type: Filter by session source table (guest, member, or administrator)
- actor_id: Filter by specific user's session (UUID matching discussion_board_guest_id, discussion_board_member_id, or discussion_board_administrator_id)
- created_at_from/created_at_to: Date range filter on created_at column
- expired_at_from/expired_at_to: Date range filter on expired_at column
- ip: Filter by client IP address for security investigations
- sort: Sort field (created_at or expired_at, default: created_at)
- order: Sort direction (asc or desc, default: desc)
- page: Page number for pagination (1-indexed, default: 1)
- limit: Records per page (1-100, default: 20)

All parameters are optional to enable flexible query construction.

- No system errors or exceptions
- Demonstrates robust handling of invalid tag references
